title: Aubergine Parmigiana Bake
description: Layers of golden fried aubergine, rich San Marzano tomato sauce, fresh basil, and bubbling melted mozzarella and Parmigiano Reggiano — a soul-warming southern Italian classic.

ingredients.name: fine sea salt
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fine sea salt (for drawing out moisture)

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.raw: 100 ml olive oil, plus extra for drizzling

ingredients.name: San Marzano tinned tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 800 g San Marzano tinned whole tomatoes

ingredients.name: fresh mozzarella
ingredients.raw: 300 g fresh mozzarella, drained and torn

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Slice the aubergines lengthways into 5 mm thick slices. Lay them in a single layer on a wire rack set over a baking tray, sprinkle generously with fine sea salt, and leave to draw out the moisture for 30 minutes. Pat thoroughly dry with kitchen paper.

While the aubergine rests, make the tomato sauce: heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a wide saucepan over a medium-low heat. Add the sliced garlic and cook gently for 2 minutes until fragrant but not coloured.

Crush the San Marzano tomatoes into the pan with your hands, then stir in the tomato purée and sugar. Season with black pepper and add a few torn basil leaves. Simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and deeply flavoured. Adjust seasoning to taste.

Heat the remaining olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine slices in batches for 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden brown. Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper to drain excess oil.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan / Gas Mark 6).
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce across the base of a deep oven dish (roughly 30 × 20 cm). Lay a single layer of fried aubergine slices on top, slightly overlapping.

Spoon over a generous layer of tomato sauce, scatter torn mozzarella and a handful of fresh basil leaves, then sprinkle with Parmigiano Reggiano. Repeat the layers — aubergine, sauce, mozzarella, basil, Parmigiano — until all the ingredients are used up, finishing with a final layer of sauce and a heavy blanket of Parmigiano Reggiano.
Drizzle lightly with olive oil and bake in the preheated oven for 30–35 minutes, until the top is deeply golden, bubbling at the edges, and the cheese is lightly caramelised.
Remove from the oven and rest for 10 minutes before serving — this helps the layers set for clean, generous portions. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and serve.
_brief: Aubergine parmigiana bake

title: Chicken Cacciatore with Olives and Peppers
description: A rustic, soul-warming Italian hunter's stew of tender braised chicken thighs simmered in a rich tomato sauce with sweet peppers, briny olives, and fragrant herbs.

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, deseeded and sliced

ingredients.name: yellow bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 yellow bell pepper, deseeded and sliced

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: small handful of fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped, to serve

steps: Pat the chicken thighs completely dry with kitchen paper, then season generously all over with salt and black pepper. Dust lightly with the plain flour, shaking off any excess.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed casserole or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs skin-side down and sear for 5–6 minutes until the skin is deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear the other side for 3 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil to the same pan. Add the sliced onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the red and yellow pepper strips and cook for a further 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened.
Pour in the white wine and use a wooden spoon to scrape up any caramelised bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it bubble and reduce for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, dried oregano, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs. Season the sauce with salt and black pepper and bring to a gentle simmer.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs back into the pan, skin-side up, ensuring they are partly submerged in the sauce. Cover with a lid and cook on a low simmer for 30 minutes.

Remove the lid, scatter in the Kalamata olives and capers, and continue to cook uncovered for a further 15 minutes, allowing the sauce to reduce and thicken and the chicken skin to crisp back up slightly.
Discard the rosemary and thyme sprigs. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve the cacciatore straight from the pan, scattered with fresh flat-leaf parsley. Accompany with crusty ciabatta, creamy polenta, or al dente tagliatelle.
_brief: Chicken cacciatore with olives and peppers

title: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragù with Pappardelle
description: A deeply rich and velvety Tuscan-style beef ragù, slow-braised in red wine and tomatoes, tossed through wide ribbons of golden pappardelle.

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 700g beef chuck, cut into 4–5 cm chunks

ingredients.name: dry red wine
ingredients.raw: 250ml dry red wine (e.g. Chianti or Barolo)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: Freshly cracked black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: Small handful of fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped, to serve

steps: Pat the beef chuck chunks completely dry with paper towels and season generously all over with fine sea salt and cracked black pepper.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed Dutch oven or casserole over a high heat. Sear the beef in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until a deep mahogany crust forms. Transfer the browned beef to a plate and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the diced onion, carrot and celery (the soffritto) and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Add the minced garlic and tomato paste, stir well to coat the vegetables, and cook for a further 2 minutes until the paste turns a deeper brick-red colour.
Pour in the red wine, scraping up any caramelised bits from the bottom of the pot. Allow the wine to bubble and reduce by half, about 4–5 minutes.
Return the seared beef to the pot. Add the crushed tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Stir to combine, ensuring the beef is mostly submerged.

Bring the ragù to a gentle simmer, then cover with a tight-fitting lid, reduce the heat to very low and cook for 3 hours, turning the beef pieces once halfway through, until the meat is completely tender and falling apart.

Remove the rosemary, thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Using two forks, shred the beef directly in the pot into coarse, generous threads. Stir in the whole milk — a traditional Italian technique that rounds out the acidity — and simmer uncovered on low for a further 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Taste the ragù and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Cook the pappardelle according to packet instructions until al dente, then reserve 1 cup of starchy pasta water before draining.
Add the drained pappardelle directly to the ragù pot. Toss vigorously over a low heat, adding a splash of reserved pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce and coat every ribbon.
Divide immediately into warm deep bowls. Finish with a generous grating of Parmigiano-Reggiano, a scatter of fresh parsley and a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil. Serve at once.
_brief: Slow-cooked beef ragù with pappardelle

title: Creamy Mushroom and Thyme Risotto
description: A velvety, restaurant-worthy Italian risotto laden with golden mushrooms, fragrant fresh thyme, and finished with a generous handful of Parmesan for pure comfort in a bowl.

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms (chestnut and portobello), sliced
ingredients.raw: 400 g mixed mushrooms (chestnut and portobello), sliced

ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped, to garnish

steps: Pour the vegetable stock into a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. Keep it warm throughout cooking — adding cold stock will arrest the cooking of the rice.

In a large, wide, heavy-bottomed pan (or Dutch oven), heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil and 20 g of the butter over medium-high heat. Once foaming, add the sliced mushrooms in a single layer. Fry undisturbed for 3 minutes until deeply golden, then toss and cook for a further 2 minutes. Strip the leaves from 3 thyme sprigs and stir them in. Season with salt and pepper, then remove the mushrooms to a plate and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan. Add the shallots with a pinch of salt and sauté gently for 4–5 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and remaining thyme sprigs and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Add the arborio rice and stir constantly for 2 minutes, toasting the grains until the edges turn slightly translucent and the rice smells nutty.
Pour in the white wine and stir vigorously until it is completely absorbed by the rice, about 1–2 minutes.

Begin adding the warm stock one ladleful (approximately 100 ml) at a time, stirring constantly and only adding the next ladle once the previous one has been fully absorbed. Continue this process for 18–20 minutes until the rice is al dente — tender with a very slight bite at the centre.

Remove the thyme sprigs. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cooked mushrooms, reserving a few for garnish. Add the double cream, the remaining 40 g of cold butter, and the grated Parmesan. Stir vigorously for 1–2 minutes (the Italian 'mantecatura' technique) until the risotto is glossy, creamy, and flows like lava when the pan is tilted. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Remove from heat and rest for 1 minute. Serve in warmed bowls topped with the reserved mushrooms, a scatter of fresh parsley, an extra grating of Parmesan, and a crack of black pepper.
_brief: Creamy mushroom and thyme risotto

title: Linguine ai Frutti di Mare con Vino Bianco, Aglio e Peperoncino
description: A gloriously authentic Italian seafood linguine where plump mussels, clams and prawns are bathed in a fragrant white wine, garlic and chilli sauce that clings beautifully to every strand.

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 200g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: fresh red chilli, finely sliced (seeds in for more heat)
ingredients.raw: 1 fresh red chilli, finely sliced (seeds in for more heat)

ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Discard any mussels or clams that are cracked or remain open when tapped firmly on a work surface. Rinse all shellfish under cold running water.

Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a rolling boil. Cook the linguine for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions (it will finish cooking in the sauce). Reserve 150ml of pasta cooking water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a large, wide pan or skillet over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli and gently sauté for 1–2 minutes until golden and fragrant — do not let the garlic burn.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, pressing them lightly to release their juices.

Increase the heat to high. Add the mussels and clams, pour in the white wine, and immediately cover with a tight-fitting lid. Steam for 3–4 minutes, shaking the pan once or twice, until all the shells have opened. Discard any that remain closed.
Add the king prawns to the pan, stir them into the sauce, and cook uncovered for 1–2 minutes until they are pink and just cooked through.
Add the drained linguine directly to the pan. Toss vigorously over a medium-high heat for 1–2 minutes, adding splashes of the reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce and help it coat every strand.
Remove from the heat. Add the lemon zest, a squeeze of lemon juice, and the chopped flat-leaf parsley. Toss once more and season with salt and black pepper.
Divide immediately between two warm shallow bowls and serve with extra lemon wedges on the side. Do not add cheese — this is authentic Italian style!
_brief: Seafood linguine with white wine, garlic and chilli

title: Gnocchi with Sage Butter and Crispy Pancetta
description: Pillowy homemade potato gnocchi tossed in a nutty golden sage butter and crowned with shards of crispy pancetta — a rustic Italian classic that's pure comfort on a plate.

ingredients.name: floury potatoes (e.g. Maris Piper or Russet)
ingredients.raw: 800g floury potatoes (e.g. Maris Piper or Russet)

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.raw: 200g plain flour, plus extra for dusting

ingredients.name: pancetta
ingredients.raw: 120g pancetta, cut into small lardons or cubes

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.raw: 40g Parmesan, finely grated, plus extra to serve

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Boil the potatoes whole and unpeeled in a large pot of salted water for 25–30 minutes until completely tender when pierced with a skewer. Drain and leave to steam-dry for 5 minutes.

While still warm, peel the potatoes and pass them through a potato ricer or fine sieve onto a clean work surface. Spread them out and allow the steam to escape for 2 minutes — drier potatoes make lighter gnocchi.

Make a well in the centre of the riced potato. Add the egg yolk, fine sea salt, nutmeg, and three-quarters of the flour. Gently bring together with your hands, adding the remaining flour little by little, until a soft, slightly tacky dough forms. Do not over-knead.

Dust the work surface lightly with flour. Divide the dough into 6 portions and roll each into a long rope about 1.5 cm thick. Cut each rope into 2 cm pieces. For the classic ridged finish, roll each piece gently over the back of a fork. Place on a lightly floured tray.

Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil. Meanwhile, place the pancetta in a cold dry frying pan, then set over medium heat. Cook for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Discard the excess fat but leave the pan on the heat.

Add the butter and crushed garlic clove to the pancetta pan over medium heat. Once the butter begins to foam, add the sage leaves. Cook for 2–3 minutes, swirling the pan, until the sage is crisp and the butter turns a light golden-brown (beurre noisette). Remove and discard the garlic clove. Remove the sage leaves and set aside — keep the brown butter in the pan over very low heat.

Working in two batches, drop the gnocchi into the boiling water. Cook for 1–2 minutes after they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon, transferring them directly into the sage butter pan.
Toss the gnocchi gently in the brown butter over medium heat for 1 minute until lightly coated and just beginning to colour at the edges.

Divide the gnocchi between two warm bowls. Scatter over the crispy pancetta lardons and the fried sage leaves. Finish with a generous grating of Parmesan, a crack of black pepper, and a pinch of flaky sea salt. Serve immediately.
_brief: Gnocchi with sage butter and crispy pancetta

title: Coq au Vin with Smoked Bacon and Mushrooms
description: A rich, soul-warming French classic of tender chicken braised in red wine with crispy smoked bacon, earthy mushrooms, and fragrant herbs.

ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
ingredients.raw: 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks (about 1.2 kg total)

ingredients.name: full-bodied red wine (e.g. Burgundy or Pinot Noir)
ingredients.raw: 500 ml full-bodied red wine (e.g. Burgundy or Pinot Noir)

ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Season the chicken pieces generously all over with salt and freshly ground black pepper, then dust lightly with the plain flour, shaking off any excess.

Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based casserole dish (Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces skin-side down for 4–5 minutes until deep golden, then flip and brown the other side for 2–3 minutes. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the bacon lardons to the same casserole. Fry for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until crispy and the fat has rendered. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside with the chicken.
Add the whole shallots to the casserole and cook in the bacon fat for 5 minutes, turning until golden all over. Add the minced garlic and cook for a further 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Bring to a boil and let it bubble for 3 minutes to cook off the alcohol.

Pour in the chicken stock, then return the browned chicken and bacon to the casserole. Add the thyme sprigs and bay leaves, ensuring the chicken is mostly submerged in the liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid and cook over low heat for 45 minutes, turning the chicken once halfway through.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a frying pan over high heat. Add the mushrooms and sauté for 5–6 minutes without stirring too much, until golden brown. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.

After 45 minutes, remove the lid from the casserole and stir in the sautéed mushrooms. Continue to simmer uncovered for a further 15 minutes to allow the sauce to reduce and thicken to a glossy, coating consistency.
Discard the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve the coq au vin in deep bowls or plates, scattered with chopped fresh parsley. Accompany with crusty French bread, buttered egg noodles, or creamy mashed potato.
_brief: Coq au vin with smoked bacon and mushrooms

title: Beef Bourguignon with Buttery Mash
description: A deeply rich, slow-braised French beef stew in a velvety Burgundy wine sauce, served over clouds of buttery mashed potato.

ingredients.name: Burgundy or Pinot Noir red wine
ingredients.raw: 375ml Burgundy or Pinot Noir red wine (half bottle)

ingredients.name: smoked lardons or bacon
ingredients.raw: 100g smoked lardons or diced smoked bacon

ingredients.name: bouquet garni
ingredients.raw: 1 bouquet garni (bay leaf, thyme, parsley stalks tied together)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: small handful of fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped (to serve)

ingredients.name: floury potatoes
ingredients.raw: 500g floury potatoes (e.g. Maris Piper or King Edward), peeled and quartered

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.raw: 80g cold unsalted butter, cubed (for the mash)

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.raw: fine salt, to taste (for the mash)

steps: Pat the beef cubes completely dry with kitchen paper. Season generously all over with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed casserole or Dutch oven over high heat. Sear the beef in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until deeply browned on all sides. Do not crowd the pan. Transfer each batch to a plate and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the lardons to the same pan and fry for 3–4 minutes until golden and the fat has rendered. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside with the beef.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the pan. Add the pearl onions and carrots, and sauté for 5 minutes until lightly coloured. Add the garlic and cook for 1 further minute.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1 minute, then scatter over the flour and stir well to coat the vegetables.
Pour in the red wine, scraping up all the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a vigorous simmer and cook for 5 minutes.

Return the seared beef and lardons to the pan. Pour over the beef stock — the liquid should just cover the meat. Nestle in the bouquet garni. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover with a tight-fitting lid.
Cook over the lowest heat (or in an oven preheated to 160°C / 140°C fan) for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is completely tender and yielding.

After 2 hours, heat 30g butter in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Sauté the mushrooms for 4–5 minutes until golden. Season and add to the casserole. Simmer uncovered for a further 15–20 minutes until the sauce has reduced to a glossy, coating consistency. Remove the bouquet garni and taste for seasoning.

Meanwhile, make the mash: place the potatoes in a large pan of well-salted cold water. Bring to the boil and cook for 18–20 minutes until completely tender. Drain thoroughly and leave to steam-dry in the colander for 2 minutes.

Pass the potatoes through a ricer or push through a fine sieve back into the warm pan. Gently heat the mash while gradually beating in the cold butter cube by cube until silky and glossy. Pour in the warm milk and beat until perfectly smooth. Season generously with fine salt.
Spoon a generous mound of buttery mash into the centre of each warmed bowl. Ladle the beef bourguignon over the top and finish with a scattering of fresh flat-leaf parsley. Serve immediately.
_brief: Beef bourguignon with buttery mash

title: Salmon en Papillote with Fennel and Lemon
description: Tender salmon fillets steamed to perfection in parchment parcels with silky fennel, bright lemon, fragrant tarragon, and a splash of white wine — a classic French technique that locks in every drop of flavour.

ingredients.name: salmon fillets, skin on
ingredients.raw: 2 salmon fillets, skin on (approx. 180 g each)

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.raw: 1 lemon, half sliced into thin rounds, half juiced

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.raw: 4 tbsp dry white wine (e.g. Sauvignon Blanc)

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.raw: 20 g unsalted butter, cut into small cubes

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to season

steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan / Gas 6).
Trim the fennel bulb, remove the tough outer layer, and slice it very thinly lengthways using a sharp knife or mandoline. Reserve a small handful of the feathery fronds for garnish.

Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the shallots, garlic, and sliced fennel with a pinch of salt and sauté for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly golden. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Cut two large rectangles of baking parchment, each roughly 40 × 30 cm. Fold each sheet in half and then open them out again — you will build the parcel on one half.
Drizzle the centre of each parchment half with a little of the remaining olive oil. Divide the sautéed fennel mixture between the two sheets, piling it in the centre.
Lay a salmon fillet, skin-side down, on top of each fennel bed. Season generously with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Place 2–3 lemon slices over each fillet, add 2 tarragon sprigs, and dot with the butter cubes.
Spoon 2 tbsp of white wine and a squeeze of lemon juice over each fillet.

Fold the empty half of the parchment over the salmon. Starting at one corner, make small, overlapping folds all along the open edges to create a tightly sealed, half-moon parcel — the parcels must be well sealed to trap steam.
Place the parcels on a baking tray and bake in the preheated oven for 12–14 minutes, until the parcels are puffed and golden at the edges.

Remove from the oven and leave to rest for 1 minute. Carefully transfer each parcel to a warm dinner plate and open at the table so guests enjoy the fragrant steam. Garnish with the reserved fennel fronds and serve immediately with crusty baguette or steamed new potatoes.
_brief: Salmon en papillote with fennel and lemon

title: Classic French Onion Soup with Gruyère Toasts
description: A deeply rich, slow-caramelised onion soup crowned with crusty baguette toasts blanketed in bubbling, golden Gruyère — the definitive French bistro classic.

ingredients.name: large white onions
ingredients.raw: 1 kg large white onions (about 5–6), thinly sliced into half-moons

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.raw: 150 ml dry white wine (e.g. Chardonnay or Muscadet)

ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: baguette
ingredients.raw: 8 slices baguette, cut 2 cm thick on the diagonal

ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
ingredients.raw: 1 tsp Dijon mustard (optional, spread thinly on toasts)

steps: Place a large, heavy-based pot or Dutch oven over medium-low heat. Melt the butter with the olive oil together.

Add all the sliced onions, the caster sugar, and the salt. Stir well to coat. Cook uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring every 5–8 minutes, for 50–60 minutes until the onions are deeply caramelised, jammy, and a rich mahogany brown. Do not rush this step — low and slow is essential for authentic flavour.
Add the minced garlic, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves and cook for a further 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Pour in the white wine and cognac, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Let it bubble and reduce for 3–4 minutes until almost evaporated.

Pour in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Stir to combine, bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes. Remove and discard the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Season generously with black pepper and adjust salt to taste.

While the soup simmers, prepare the Gruyère toasts. Preheat your oven grill (broiler) to high. Arrange the baguette slices on a baking tray and grill for 1–2 minutes per side until lightly golden and crisp.
If using, spread a thin layer of Dijon mustard on one side of each toast. Top generously with grated Gruyère.
Ladle the hot soup into 4 oven-safe soup crocks or bowls, filling to about 1 cm from the top. Float 2 Gruyère toasts on top of each bowl, cheese-side up.
Place the bowls on a sturdy baking tray and slide under the hot grill for 3–5 minutes until the cheese is completely melted, bubbling, and golden brown with dark-caramelised spots.
Carefully remove from the grill — the bowls will be very hot. Allow to rest for 1 minute, then serve immediately.
_brief: French onion soup with gruyère toasts

title: Provençal Ratatouille with Herbes de Provence & Crusty Bread
description: A slow-simmered, sun-drenched Provençal vegetable stew fragrant with herbes de Provence, served alongside golden, oil-rubbed crusty bread.

ingredients.name: aubergine (eggplant)
ingredients.raw: 1 large aubergine (eggplant), cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: courgettes (zucchini)
ingredients.raw: 2 medium courgettes (zucchini), cut into 2 cm rounds

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, deseeded and cut into 2 cm chunks

ingredients.name: yellow bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 yellow bell pepper, deseeded and cut into 2 cm chunks

ingredients.name: ripe plum tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 500 g ripe plum tomatoes, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: sourdough or rustic French baguette
ingredients.raw: 1 sourdough loaf or rustic French baguette, sliced

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the bread

ingredients.name: garlic clove
ingredients.raw: 1 clove garlic, halved (for rubbing the bread)

steps: Place the cubed aubergine in a colander, sprinkle generously with flaky sea salt, toss to coat, and leave for 20 minutes to draw out moisture. Rinse well under cold water and pat thoroughly dry with kitchen paper.

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large, wide, heavy-bottomed casserole or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the aubergine in a single layer and sauté for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on all sides. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Add another tablespoon of olive oil to the same pan. Add the courgettes and cook for 3–4 minutes until lightly coloured. Transfer to the plate with the aubergine.
Add another tablespoon of olive oil and sauté the red and yellow peppers for 4–5 minutes until softened and slightly charred at the edges. Transfer to the plate.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil. Add the sliced onion and cook gently for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until completely softened and translucent. Add the sliced garlic and cook for a further 2 minutes until fragrant.

Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1 minute. Add the chopped plum tomatoes, herbes de Provence, bay leaves, and caster sugar. Season well with salt and black pepper. Stir to combine and bring to a gentle simmer.

Return all the sautéed vegetables to the casserole and gently fold them into the tomato base. Reduce the heat to low, partially cover with a lid, and simmer slowly for 30–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are very tender and the sauce has thickened and become rich. Taste and adjust seasoning.

While the ratatouille finishes cooking, preheat your grill (broiler) to high. Slice the bread, brush each slice with extra-virgin olive oil, and grill for 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. Immediately rub the cut side of the halved garlic clove over the hot toast.

Remove the bay leaves from the ratatouille. Scatter over the torn basil and chopped parsley. Serve the ratatouille in warm shallow bowls or directly from the casserole at the table, with the garlic-rubbed crusty bread alongside for mopping up the rich sauce.
_brief: Ratatouille with herbes de Provence and crusty bread

title: Slow-Roast Greek Lamb Shoulder with Lemon Potatoes
description: A meltingly tender bone-in lamb shoulder slow-roasted with garlic, oregano and rosemary, resting on golden lemon-kissed potatoes soaked in fragrant pan juices — pure, soul-warming Greek taverna cooking.

ingredients.name: Maris Piper potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1.2 kg Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and cut into large wedges

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped, to serve

steps: Remove the lamb shoulder from the fridge 1 hour before cooking to bring it to room temperature. Preheat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan / Gas 7).

Peel 4 of the garlic cloves and cut each into 3 slivers. Using a small sharp knife, make 12 deep incisions all over the lamb shoulder and push a sliver of garlic and a small sprig of rosemary into each one.
In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp of the dried oregano, salt and pepper to make a marinade. Rub this all over the lamb, coating it thoroughly.

Peel and lightly crush the remaining 4 garlic cloves and scatter them into a large, deep roasting tin. Add the potato wedges, the juice of 1 lemon, the remaining 1 tbsp oregano, white wine, chicken stock, thyme sprigs and the squeezed lemon halves. Season generously with salt and pepper and toss everything together.
Place the marinated lamb shoulder directly on top of the potatoes in the roasting tin. Roast uncovered at 220 °C for 20 minutes until the lamb is nicely browned on the outside.
Reduce the oven temperature to 160 °C (140 °C fan / Gas 3). Cover the roasting tin very tightly with a double layer of foil. Slow-roast for 3 hours 30 minutes.

Remove the foil and baste the lamb and potatoes well with the pan juices. Squeeze the juice of the remaining lemon over the potatoes and dot the butter over the lamb. Return to the oven uncovered for a final 30 minutes until the lamb is deeply golden and falling off the bone, and the potatoes are caramelised at the edges.
Remove from the oven and rest, loosely tented with foil, for 15 minutes. Use two forks to pull the tender lamb apart into large, rustic chunks directly in the tin.
Scatter generously with fresh flat-leaf parsley and serve straight from the roasting tin with crusty bread or a simple Greek salad.
_brief: Slow-roast Greek lamb shoulder with lemon potatoes

title: Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki and Warm Flatbreads
description: Juicy lemon-and-herb marinated chicken skewers served with cool, garlicky tzatziki and pillowy warm flatbreads — a classic Greek feast straight from the taverna.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.raw: 600g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3cm chunks

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.name: cucumber
ingredients.raw: ½ cucumber, grated and squeezed dry

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.raw: 250g plain flour, plus extra for dusting

ingredients.name: wooden or metal skewers
ingredients.raw: 6 wooden or metal skewers (if wooden, soak for 30 mins)

steps: Marinate the chicken: In a large bowl, whisk together 4 tbsp olive oil, 3 tbsp lemon juice, 3 minced garlic cloves, oregano, cumin, paprika, 1 tsp salt, and black pepper. Add the chicken chunks and toss well to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or up to 8 hours for maximum flavour.

Make the tzatziki: Grate the cucumber and wrap it tightly in a clean tea towel, squeezing out as much liquid as possible. In a bowl, combine the Greek yoghurt, squeezed cucumber, 2 minced garlic cloves, fresh dill, 1 tbsp olive oil, and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Season with salt, stir well, cover and refrigerate until serving.

Make the flatbread dough: In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and ½ tsp salt. Add the 150g Greek yoghurt and 1 tbsp olive oil, then mix until a soft dough forms. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 2 minutes until smooth. Divide into 4 equal balls.
Roll the flatbreads: On a floured surface, roll each dough ball into a thin oval roughly 20cm long and 3–4mm thick.
Thread the chicken: Divide the marinated chicken evenly among the 6 skewers, packing the pieces snugly together.

Cook the souvlaki: Heat a griddle pan or barbecue over high heat. Grill the chicken skewers for 10–12 minutes total, turning every 3–4 minutes, until nicely charred on the outside and cooked through with no pink remaining. Rest for 2 minutes.

Cook the flatbreads: While the chicken rests, heat a dry frying pan or griddle over medium-high heat. Cook each flatbread for 2 minutes per side until puffed, golden, and lightly charred. Keep warm wrapped in a clean tea towel.

Assemble and serve: Spread a generous dollop of tzatziki onto each warm flatbread, slide the chicken off the skewers on top, and finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon. Serve immediately with any remaining tzatziki alongside.
_brief: Chicken souvlaki with tzatziki and warm flatbreads

title: Baked Prawn Saganaki with Tomato and Feta
description: Plump prawns nestled in a rich, herb-scented tomato sauce and crowned with crumbled feta, baked until bubbling for a classic taste of the Greek taverna.

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 500g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: black pepper, freshly ground
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 3 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: crusty bread or warm pita, to serve
ingredients.raw: crusty bread or warm pita, to serve

steps: Preheat your oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C / Gas 6).
Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe frying pan or shallow casserole dish over a medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 6–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and translucent.
Add the sliced garlic and chopped chilli and cook for a further 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes to cook off the alcohol.

Stir in the tinned tomatoes, cherry tomatoes, tomato paste, dried oregano, and sugar. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Simmer over a medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Remove the pan from the heat. Nestle the raw king prawns evenly into the tomato sauce in a single layer.
Scatter the crumbled feta generously and evenly over the top.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven and bake for 12–15 minutes, until the prawns are pink and cooked through and the feta has softened and turned golden at the edges.
Remove from the oven, scatter with freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, and serve immediately straight from the pan with crusty bread or warm pita to mop up the sauce.
_brief: Baked prawn saganaki with tomato and feta

title: Spanakopita — Greek Spinach & Feta Filo Pie
description: A golden, shatteringly crisp filo pie packed with wilted spinach, creamy feta, fresh herbs, and a whisper of nutmeg — straight from a Greek kitchen to your table.

ingredients.name: fresh spinach
ingredients.raw: 900 g fresh spinach, washed and tough stems removed

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 20 g fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: filo pastry sheets
ingredients.raw: 270 g filo pastry (approx. 12 sheets), thawed if frozen

steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) fan. Lightly grease a 33 × 23 cm (13 × 9 in) baking dish with a little melted butter.

Wilt the spinach in batches in a large dry pan over high heat until just collapsed, about 2 minutes per batch. Transfer to a colander and leave to cool. Once cool enough to handle, squeeze out as much liquid as possible with your hands or a clean tea towel, then roughly chop.

Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Sauté the diced yellow onion for 6–7 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and spring onions and cook for a further 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and allow to cool slightly.

In a large bowl, combine the crumbled feta, ricotta, beaten eggs, nutmeg, black pepper, dill, and parsley. Mix well. Fold in the chopped spinach and the cooled onion mixture. Taste and season with salt if needed (feta is already salty, so go carefully).

Mix the melted butter with a brush. Lay one sheet of filo in the prepared dish, allowing any overhang to drape over the sides. Brush generously with melted butter. Repeat with 5 more sheets, brushing each one, to form the base.
Spoon the spinach and feta filling evenly over the filo base and spread level with a spatula.

Layer the remaining 6 filo sheets on top, brushing every sheet with melted butter as you go. Fold any overhanging edges up and over the top to form a neat border, pressing lightly to seal. Brush the top with any remaining butter.
Using a sharp knife, score the top layers of filo into 6–8 portions (do not cut all the way through). Scatter over the sesame seeds if using.
Bake in the preheated oven for 40–45 minutes until the top is deeply golden and crisp.
Remove from the oven and leave to rest for 10 minutes before cutting through completely and serving. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
_brief: Spanakopita — spinach and feta filo pie

title: Steak and Ale Pie with Shortcrust Lid
description: A deeply satisfying British classic — slow-braised beef and rich ale gravy crowned with a golden, buttery shortcrust pastry lid.

ingredients.name: beef chuck steak
ingredients.raw: 700g beef chuck steak, cut into 3cm chunks

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.raw: 2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks

ingredients.name: dark ale
ingredients.raw: 330ml dark ale (e.g. Newcastle Brown or London Pride)

steps: Toss the beef chunks in the 3 tbsp of plain flour seasoned generously with salt and black pepper until well coated.

Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-based casserole dish over a high heat. Brown the beef in batches for 3–4 minutes per batch, ensuring a deep crust forms on all sides. Remove each batch and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining oil and the 20g of butter to the same pan. Fry the onion, carrots and celery for 6–7 minutes until softened and beginning to colour. Add the garlic and tomato purée and cook for a further 1 minute.
Return the browned beef to the pan. Pour in the ale and let it bubble for 2 minutes to cook off the raw alcohol, scraping up any sticky bits from the bottom of the pan.

Add the beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Stir well, bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook on a low heat for 1 hour 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick and glossy. Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaves, taste and adjust seasoning, then transfer the filling to a deep 20cm pie dish and leave to cool completely.

While the filling cools, make the shortcrust pastry. Add the 220g flour and a pinch of salt to a large bowl. Rub in the cold cubed butter with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.

Add cold water one tablespoon at a time, mixing with a butter knife after each addition, until the dough just comes together. Shape into a disc, wrap in cling film and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan / Gas 6).
On a lightly floured surface, roll the pastry out to roughly 3–4mm thick — large enough to cover the top of your pie dish with a 2cm overhang all around.

Brush the rim of the pie dish with beaten egg. Drape the pastry over the filling, press it firmly to the rim to seal, and trim away any excess with a sharp knife. Crimp the edges with a fork or your fingers for a decorative finish.
Brush the pastry lid all over with the beaten egg wash. Cut two small slits in the centre to allow steam to escape.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30–35 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
_brief: Steak and ale pie with a shortcrust lid

title: Classic British Cottage Pie with Cheddar Mash
description: A deeply comforting British classic of rich, slow-cooked minced beef in a savoury gravy, crowned with a golden, bubbling cheddar mash crust.

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: Maris Piper potatoes
ingredients.raw: 900 g Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

ingredients.name: mature cheddar
ingredients.raw: 120 g mature cheddar, grated (plus extra for topping)

steps: Preheat your oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan / gas mark 6).
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery, and fry gently for 8–10 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for a further minute until fragrant.
Increase the heat to medium-high, add the beef mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring frequently, until deeply browned all over.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes. Add the Worcestershire sauce, pour in the beef stock, and add the bay leaves and thyme sprigs.

Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and richly reduced. Stir in the frozen peas for the final 2 minutes. Season generously with salt and pepper. Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs, then transfer the mince to a deep 22 cm × 28 cm ovenproof dish.
Meanwhile, cook the potato chunks in a large pan of salted boiling water for 15–18 minutes until completely tender. Drain well and leave to steam-dry in the colander for 2 minutes.
Return the potatoes to the pan. Mash until smooth, then beat in the butter, warm milk, English mustard and 100 g of the grated cheddar. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon the cheddar mash evenly over the beef filling. Use a fork to create ridges across the surface — these will crisp up beautifully in the oven.
Scatter the remaining 20 g of cheddar over the top. Bake on the middle shelf for 25–30 minutes until the topping is golden and the filling is bubbling around the edges.
Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve with steamed green beans or peas on the side.
_brief: Cottage pie with cheddar mash

title: Toad in the Hole with Rich Onion Gravy
description: Plump, golden pork sausages baked in a gloriously puffed Yorkshire pudding batter, served with a deep, sticky onion gravy — the ultimate British comfort dinner.

ingredients.name: onions
ingredients.raw: 3 large onions, peeled and thinly sliced

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Make the batter first so it can rest. Sift the plain flour and salt into a large bowl and make a well in the centre. Crack in the eggs and the mustard, then whisk together, gradually drawing in the flour from the sides.

Slowly pour in the milk and cold water, whisking continuously until you have a completely smooth, lump-free batter with the consistency of single cream. Season with black pepper. Cover and leave to rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.

While the batter rests, make the onion gravy. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a wide, heavy-based saucepan over a medium-low heat. Add the sliced onions, thyme sprigs, sugar, and a good pinch of salt. Stir well, then cook slowly for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onions are deeply golden, soft, and caramelised.

Stir the tablespoon of plain flour into the caramelised onions and cook for 1 minute. Add the Worcestershire sauce, then gradually pour in the beef stock, stirring constantly. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes until the gravy is glossy and slightly thickened. Remove the thyme sprigs, season to taste, and keep warm on the lowest heat.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C / 200 °C fan / Gas Mark 7. Pour the sunflower oil into a large, deep roasting tin (roughly 30 × 25 cm) and place it in the oven for 5 minutes to heat.
Add the sausages to the hot, oiled tin and return to the oven for 15 minutes, turning once halfway, until lightly browned all over.

Working quickly, pull the oven shelf out and carefully pour the rested batter all around and between the sausages in one confident pour. Immediately slide the tin back into the oven and close the door — do not open it for at least 25 minutes.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the batter is dramatically puffed, deep golden brown, and crisp around the edges. Resist opening the oven during baking or the batter will collapse.
Remove from the oven and serve immediately, cut into generous portions, with the warm onion gravy ladled generously over the top.
_brief: Toad in the hole with onion gravy

title: British Fish Pie with Leeks and Dill
description: A comforting classic British fish pie packed with flaky salmon, smoked haddock, and king prawns nestled in a creamy dill sauce with sweet leeks, all crowned with a golden, buttery mashed potato topping.

ingredients.name: Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and cubed
ingredients.raw: 800g Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and cubed

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan / Gas 6).

Pour the 400ml milk into a wide saucepan and add the bay leaf and peppercorns. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then add the salmon and smoked haddock. Poach for 5 minutes until just cooked through. Remove the fish with a slotted spoon and set aside on a plate. Strain and reserve the poaching milk, discarding the bay leaf and peppercorns.
Once cool enough to handle, flake the poached fish into large chunks, checking for any remaining bones. Set aside with the raw king prawns.

Cook the potatoes in a large pan of salted boiling water for 15–18 minutes until completely tender. Drain thoroughly and leave to steam-dry for 2 minutes, then mash until smooth. Beat in the 40g butter and 60ml milk, then stir in the egg yolk. Season well with salt and white pepper. Set aside.
Melt the 60g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the sliced leeks and a pinch of salt, and sauté gently for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until completely softened but not browned.

Stir the plain flour into the leeks and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Gradually pour in the reserved poaching milk, a little at a time, stirring vigorously after each addition to prevent lumps. Once all the milk is incorporated, add the double cream and Dijon mustard. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy. Remove from the heat and stir in the fresh dill. Season with salt and white pepper.

Gently fold the flaked fish and raw king prawns into the leek sauce, taking care not to break up the fish too much. Pour the mixture into a deep oven-proof dish (approximately 1.5 litre capacity) and spread evenly.

Spoon the mashed potato over the fish filling and spread it gently to the edges to seal. Use a fork to create a ridged pattern across the top (this helps the peaks turn golden and crisp). Scatter over the grated Cheddar.
Place the pie dish on a baking tray and bake in the preheated oven for 25–30 minutes, until the top is deeply golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
Remove from the oven and leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve with steamed garden peas or tenderstem broccoli.
_brief: Fish pie with leeks and dill

title: Chicken, Leek & Tarragon Pie
description: A gloriously golden, buttery shortcrust pie packed with tender chicken, sweet leeks and fragrant tarragon in a velvety cream sauce — pure British comfort on a plate.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.raw: 300g plain flour, plus extra for dusting

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.raw: 1 egg, beaten (for pastry and egg wash)

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.raw: 600g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3cm chunks

ingredients.name: leeks
ingredients.raw: 3 medium leeks, trimmed, washed and sliced into 1cm rounds

ingredients.name: fresh tarragon
ingredients.raw: 3 tbsp fresh tarragon leaves, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to season

steps: Make the shortcrust pastry: tip 300g flour and a pinch of salt into a large bowl. Add the cold cubed butter and rub together with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Add half the beaten egg and the cold water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing with a palette knife until the dough just comes together. Wrap in cling film and rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / Gas Mark 6. Season the chicken thigh pieces all over with salt and pepper.

Heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over a high heat. Brown the chicken pieces in batches for 3–4 minutes until golden, then remove to a plate. They do not need to be fully cooked through at this stage.

Reduce the heat to medium and melt the 30g butter in the same pan. Add the leeks and a pinch of salt, and sweat gently for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until completely softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further 1 minute.
Stir in the 2 tbsp flour and cook for 1 minute to form a roux. Gradually pour in the chicken stock, stirring constantly to avoid lumps, then stir in the double cream.

Return the browned chicken to the pan, add the Dijon mustard and tarragon, and stir well. Simmer gently for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Taste and adjust seasoning. Transfer the filling to a 24cm pie dish and leave to cool for 15 minutes.

Lightly flour a work surface and divide the rested pastry into two-thirds and one-third. Roll the larger piece out to roughly 3mm thick and large enough to line the base and sides of the pie dish with a small overhang. Carefully drape it over the dish, pressing gently into the edges.

Roll the remaining pastry into a lid. Brush the pastry rim with a little of the remaining beaten egg, then lay the lid on top. Press the edges firmly together to seal, then trim any excess and crimp with a fork or your fingers.
Brush the entire pastry surface generously with the remaining beaten egg. Cut two small slits in the centre to allow steam to escape.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30–35 minutes until the pastry is deep golden brown and the filling is piping hot. Rest for 5 minutes before serving with buttered greens and mashed potato.
_brief: Chicken, leek and tarragon pie

title: Sausage & Butter Bean Bake with Rosemary
description: Hearty British banger sausages nestled in creamy butter beans with fragrant rosemary, smoky bacon, and a rich tomato gravy — the ultimate comforting one-pot bake.

ingredients.name: butter beans
ingredients.raw: 400 g tin of butter beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Preheat your oven to 200 °C / 180 °C fan / Gas Mark 6.

Heat the olive oil in a large, ovenproof casserole dish or deep skillet over a medium-high heat. Add the sausages and brown them all over for about 5 minutes, turning regularly. Remove and set aside — they don't need to be cooked through at this stage.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry for 3–4 minutes until the fat begins to render and the lardons are lightly golden.
Add the sliced onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to caramelise. Add the garlic and fry for a further 1 minute until fragrant.
Strip the leaves from one rosemary sprig and finely chop them. Stir the chopped rosemary, Worcestershire sauce, and Dijon mustard into the pan.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Stir well, then add the drained butter beans. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Nestle the browned sausages back into the pan and lay the remaining whole rosemary sprig on top.
Transfer the dish to the preheated oven and bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes until the sauce is thickened and bubbling and the sausages are cooked through and slightly glazed on top.
Remove the whole rosemary sprig, taste and adjust seasoning, then serve straight from the dish with plenty of crusty bread to mop up the sauce.
_brief: Sausage and butter bean bake with rosemary

title: Chicken & Chorizo Paella
description: A sun-drenched Spanish classic bursting with smoky chorizo, golden chicken, saffron-kissed rice, and sweet roasted peppers — all cooked in one glorious pan.

ingredients.name: vine tomatoes, grated or finely chopped
ingredients.raw: 3 vine tomatoes, grated or finely chopped

ingredients.name: flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Steep the saffron threads in 4 tbsp of the hot chicken stock and set aside for at least 10 minutes to bloom.
Season the chicken thighs generously on both sides with salt, black pepper, and 1 tsp of the smoked paprika.

Heat the olive oil in a large, wide paella pan (or a wide, shallow oven-safe frying pan) over medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs skin-side down and sear for 5–6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp. Flip and sear the other side for 3 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add the chorizo slices to the same pan and fry for 2–3 minutes until they release their orange oil and start to crisp at the edges. Remove and set aside with the chicken.
Reduce the heat to medium. In the remaining oil, add the onion and peppers. Sauté for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly caramelised.
Add the garlic and remaining 1 tsp of smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the grated tomatoes and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the mixture darkens and most of the liquid has evaporated — this is the sofrito base.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble and reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Add the paella rice and stir to coat thoroughly in the sofrito for 1–2 minutes.
Pour in the remaining hot chicken stock and the saffron-infused stock. Stir everything together well, then taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs and chorizo slices back into the pan, distributing evenly. Bring to a steady simmer.

Once simmering, do NOT stir the paella again. Cook uncovered on a medium-low heat for 18–20 minutes until the rice has absorbed nearly all the stock and the chicken is cooked through (internal temp 75°C/165°F).
For the authentic socarrat (toasted crust), increase the heat to high for the final 1–2 minutes — you should hear a gentle crackle. Watch carefully to avoid burning.
Remove the pan from the heat, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 5 minutes.
Scatter generously with fresh parsley and serve straight from the pan with lemon wedges on the side.
_brief: Chicken and chorizo paella

title: Zarzuela de Mariscos – Spanish Saffron & Tomato Seafood Stew
description: A deeply aromatic Catalan seafood stew brimming with prawns, mussels, squid and clams, slow-simmered in a golden saffron and roasted tomato broth that begs to be mopped up with crusty bread.

ingredients.name: large raw king prawns, shell-on
ingredients.raw: 300 g large raw king prawns, shell-on

ingredients.name: squid, cleaned and sliced into rings
ingredients.raw: 200 g squid, cleaned and sliced into rings

ingredients.name: black pepper, freshly ground
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Bloom the saffron: place the saffron threads in a small bowl, pour over 3 tbsp of warm fish stock, and leave to steep for at least 10 minutes.

Make the sofrito: heat the olive oil in a large, deep cazuela or wide heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and red pepper to the pan and cook for a further 5 minutes until the pepper has softened.

Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes, smoked paprika and sweet paprika. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, for 12–15 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down and the sofrito is deep, thick and fragrant.
Pour in the white wine, increase the heat to medium-high and let it bubble for 2 minutes to cook off the alcohol.
Add the remaining fish stock and the saffron with its steeping liquid. Drop in the bay leaves, stir well and bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the squid rings to the broth and cook for 5 minutes.
Nestle the mussels and clams into the stew, cover with a lid and cook for 3–4 minutes, shaking the pan once or twice, until the shells have opened. Discard any that remain closed.
Uncover and add the king prawns, pushing them down into the broth. Replace the lid and cook for a further 3–4 minutes until the prawns are pink and just cooked through.
Remove and discard the bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter generously with flat-leaf parsley and serve straight from the cazuela with lemon wedges and plenty of crusty bread.
_brief: Spanish seafood stew with saffron and tomato

title: Spanish Pork Loin with Romesco Sauce and Roasted Peppers
description: Tender, herb-rubbed pork loin served alongside charred sweet peppers and a deep, smoky romesco sauce made the authentic Catalan way with roasted tomatoes, almonds, and ñora peppers.

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.raw: 6 cloves garlic (2 for rub, 4 for romesco)

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.raw: 1 tsp smoked paprika (pimentón de la Vera)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: red romano peppers
ingredients.raw: 3 red romano peppers, halved and deseeded

ingredients.name: yellow bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 yellow bell pepper, halved and deseeded

ingredients.name: ñora peppers (dried)
ingredients.raw: 2 dried ñora peppers (or 1 tbsp ancho chilli paste as substitute)

ingredients.name: flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped, to garnish

steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C / gas 6). Soak the dried ñora peppers in a bowl of just-boiled water for 20 minutes until softened, then drain, halve, and scrape out the flesh with a spoon; set aside.

While the peppers soak, make the herb rub: crush 2 garlic cloves to a paste with a pinch of salt, then mix with 1 tbsp olive oil, the smoked paprika, thyme leaves (stripped from 2 sprigs), salt, and black pepper. Pat the pork loin dry and rub all over with this mixture. Leave to marinate at room temperature for 15 minutes.

Place the romano peppers, yellow bell pepper, and halved tomatoes cut-side up on a large roasting tray. Nestle the remaining 4 unpeeled garlic cloves among them, drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes until softened and lightly charred at the edges.

Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in an ovenproof frying pan over high heat. Sear the marinated pork loin for 2–3 minutes on each side until golden all over. Transfer the pan to the oven and roast alongside the vegetables for 20–25 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the pork reaches 63 °C. Remove and rest under foil for 10 minutes.

While the pork rests, make the romesco: toast the almonds and hazelnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, shaking frequently, until golden. Place in a food processor with the ñora pepper flesh, the roasted tomatoes, the flesh squeezed from the roasted garlic cloves, the torn bread, sherry vinegar, and 2 tbsp olive oil. Blend to a coarse, thick sauce. Season to taste with salt and a little extra sherry vinegar if needed.

Arrange the roasted peppers on a warm serving platter. Slice the pork loin into 1.5 cm medallions and lay over the peppers. Spoon a generous stripe of romesco sauce across the pork and serve the rest alongside. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley and the remaining thyme sprigs.
_brief: Pork loin with romesco sauce and roast peppers

title: Spanish Patatas Bravas Traybake with Chorizo & Garlic Aioli
description: Smoky, crispy potatoes and sizzling chorizo roasted in a fiery bravas sauce, finished with a luscious homemade garlic aioli — a bold, authentic taste of Spain straight from your oven.

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes (e.g. Maris Piper or Desiree), cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.raw: 800g waxy potatoes (e.g. Maris Piper or Desiree), cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: cooking chorizo, sliced into 1 cm rounds
ingredients.raw: 200g cooking chorizo, sliced into 1 cm rounds

ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 1 handful fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

steps: Preheat your oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan / Gas 7). Place a large roasting tray inside to heat up.
Par-boil the potato chunks in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for 8 minutes until just starting to soften. Drain thoroughly and leave to steam-dry in the colander for 2 minutes.
In a large bowl, toss the drained potatoes with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp smoked paprika, salt and pepper until well coated.
Carefully remove the hot tray from the oven, add the potatoes in a single layer, and roast for 20 minutes, turning once halfway, until starting to turn golden.

Meanwhile, make the bravas sauce: heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the remaining smoked paprika, hot paprika and cumin and cook for 30 seconds. Pour in the passata, sherry vinegar and sugar, stir well and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season to taste and set aside.

Make the garlic aioli: crush the garlic clove to a fine paste with a pinch of fine salt using the flat of a knife. In a bowl, whisk together the egg yolk, crushed garlic and Dijon mustard. Very slowly drizzle in the extra-virgin olive oil, whisking constantly, until the mixture emulsifies into a thick, glossy aioli. Stir in the lemon juice and season to taste. Refrigerate until needed.

After the potatoes have had their initial 20 minutes, scatter the chorizo slices over the tray and return to the oven for a further 15 minutes, until the chorizo is caramelised and the potatoes are deeply golden and crisp.
Remove the tray from the oven and pour the bravas sauce over the potatoes and chorizo, tossing gently to coat everything.
Return the tray to the oven for a final 5 minutes to let the sauce meld with the potatoes.
Remove from the oven, scatter generously with fresh parsley and bring the tray straight to the table. Serve with the garlic aioli on the side for drizzling or dipping.
_brief: Patatas bravas traybake with garlic aioli and chorizo

title: Lamb Kofta with Pomegranate & Herby Couscous
description: Juicy, spiced lamb kofta skewers charred to perfection, served over a vibrant herby couscous jewelled with sweet pomegranate seeds and a cooling yoghurt drizzle.

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 20g fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped (half for kofta, half for couscous)

ingredients.name: fresh mint leaves
ingredients.raw: 15g fresh mint leaves, finely chopped (half for kofta, half for couscous)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.name: garlic clove
ingredients.raw: 1 small garlic clove, minced (for yoghurt sauce)

steps: Soak 6–8 wooden skewers in cold water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning, or use metal skewers.

In a large bowl, combine the lamb mince, grated onion, minced garlic, cumin, ground coriander, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cayenne, allspice, half the chopped parsley, half the chopped mint, salt, and black pepper. Mix firmly with your hands for 2–3 minutes until the mixture is sticky and very well combined — this is key for kofta that hold their shape.

Divide the lamb mixture into 8 equal portions. With damp hands, mould each portion firmly around a skewer into a long sausage shape, about 12 cm long. Place on a tray, cover, and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes to firm up.

While the kofta chill, make the herby couscous. Place the couscous in a large heatproof bowl and pour over the hot stock. Add 1 tbsp of olive oil and the lemon zest, stir briefly, then cover tightly with a plate or cling film and leave for 8 minutes.

Fluff the couscous with a fork, breaking up any clumps. Drizzle over the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and the lemon juice, and season well with salt and pepper. Fold in the remaining parsley, remaining mint, fresh coriander, spring onions, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pine nuts. Set aside at room temperature.
Make the yoghurt sauce by stirring the minced garlic clove into the Greek yoghurt with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon juice. Set aside.

Preheat a griddle pan, barbecue, or grill to high heat. Lightly oil the surface. Cook the kofta skewers for 8–10 minutes total, turning every 2 minutes, until deeply charred on the outside and just cooked through with no pink remaining.

Pile the herby couscous onto plates and lay the hot kofta skewers alongside. Spoon generous dollops of yoghurt sauce over the top, then drizzle everything with pomegranate molasses. Garnish with a few extra pomegranate seeds and fresh herbs if desired, and serve immediately.
_brief: Lamb kofta with pomegranate and herby couscous

title: Chicken Shawarma Bowls with Pickled Red Onion
description: Tender, warmly spiced chicken shawarma piled over fluffy rice with vibrant quick-pickled red onion, creamy garlic sauce, and fresh toppings for an irresistible Middle Eastern feast at home.

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

steps: Make the quick-pickled red onion: place the thinly sliced red onion in a bowl or jar. Pour over the red wine vinegar, add the sugar and 1/2 tsp salt, and stir well. Set aside for at least 30 minutes at room temperature — the onion will turn bright pink and mellow in flavour.

Marinate the chicken: in a large bowl, whisk together the yoghurt, 2 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, cayenne, lemon juice, salt, and black pepper. Add the chicken thighs and toss to coat thoroughly. Cover and marinate for at least 20 minutes (or up to 24 hours in the fridge).
Make the garlic sauce (toum-style): stir together the mayonnaise, plain yoghurt, minced garlic clove, and 1 tbsp lemon juice until smooth. Season to taste with salt. Refrigerate until needed.

Cook the rice: rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Bring the stock to the boil in a saucepan, add the rice, stir once, then cover and reduce to the lowest heat. Cook for 12 minutes, then remove from heat and leave covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Cook the chicken: heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan or griddle pan over medium-high heat. Remove the chicken from the marinade and cook for 5–6 minutes per side until deeply charred and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Rest for 5 minutes.
Slice the chicken: cut the rested chicken thighs into thin strips against the grain, mimicking the classic shawarma shave.
Assemble the bowls: divide the fluffy rice between two bowls. Arrange the sliced chicken, drained pickled red onion, cherry tomatoes, and diced cucumber over the rice.
Drizzle generously with the garlic sauce, scatter with fresh parsley, and dust with sumac before serving.
_brief: Chicken shawarma bowls with pickled red onion

title: Shakshuka with Feta and Harissa
description: Smoky, spiced tomato sauce spiked with fiery harissa, cradling perfectly poached eggs and crowned with creamy crumbled feta — a bold, soul-warming one-pan dinner.

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 large red bell pepper, finely diced

ingredients.name: canned whole plum tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 800 g canned whole plum tomatoes (2 × 400 g tins)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: Small handful fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: fresh mint
ingredients.raw: Small handful fresh mint, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: crusty bread or pita
ingredients.raw: Crusty bread or warm pita, to serve

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large, deep ovenproof skillet or cast-iron pan over medium heat.
Add the diced onion and red pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8–10 minutes until softened and beginning to caramelise at the edges.
Add the minced garlic and cook for a further 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the harissa paste and tomato paste, coating the vegetables well, and cook for 2 minutes to deepen the flavours.
Add the ground cumin, smoked paprika, and ground coriander. Stir and toast the spices for 30 seconds.
Pour in the canned plum tomatoes, crushing them with the back of a wooden spoon. Add the sugar, season generously with salt and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer the sauce, uncovered, for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens and the oil begins to separate at the surface.
Taste and adjust seasoning or harissa level to your preference.
Use the back of a spoon to make 4 evenly spaced wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
Scatter half the crumbled feta over the sauce between the eggs.
Cover the pan with a lid (or foil) and cook over medium-low heat for 6–8 minutes, until the egg whites are just set but the yolks remain runny.
Remove from the heat, scatter over the remaining feta, fresh parsley, and mint.
Serve immediately straight from the pan with plenty of crusty bread or warm pita for scooping.
_brief: Shakshuka with feta and harissa

title: Roast Cauliflower with Tahini, Chickpeas and Zhoug
description: A stunning Yemeni-inspired platter of golden caramelised cauliflower and crispy chickpeas, drizzled with silky lemon tahini and a fiery, fragrant coriander zhoug.

ingredients.name: cauliflower
ingredients.raw: 1 large head of cauliflower, cut into large florets

ingredients.name: canned chickpeas
ingredients.raw: 400 g canned chickpeas, drained and dried well

ingredients.name: fresh green chillies
ingredients.raw: 2 fresh green chillies (e.g. serrano or jalapeño), roughly chopped

ingredients.name: toasted pine nuts
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts, to serve

steps: Preheat your oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan / gas 7) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.

Make the zhoug: place the fresh coriander, parsley, green chillies, garlic, cardamom, cumin, olive oil, lemon juice and salt into a small food processor or blender. Blitz to a vivid, textured sauce. Taste and adjust salt or chilli heat. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Make the lemon tahini: whisk together the tahini, lemon juice and grated garlic. Gradually whisk in the ice-cold water one tablespoon at a time until you have a smooth, pourable, creamy sauce. Season with salt and set aside.

Prepare the cauliflower and chickpeas: in a large bowl, combine the olive oil, cumin, ground coriander, smoked paprika, turmeric and sea salt. Add the cauliflower florets and pat-dry chickpeas and toss well until everything is evenly coated in the spiced oil.

Spread the cauliflower florets in a single layer on one baking tray and the chickpeas on the other. Roast for 35–40 minutes, turning the cauliflower halfway and shaking the chickpeas once, until the cauliflower is deeply golden and charred at the edges and the chickpeas are crispy.
To assemble: swirl the lemon tahini generously over a large serving platter. Arrange the roasted cauliflower on top, then scatter over the crispy chickpeas.
Spoon vibrant green zhoug liberally over the cauliflower, then finish with pomegranate seeds and toasted pine nuts.
Serve immediately with warm flatbreads to scoop everything up.
_brief: Roast cauliflower with tahini, chickpeas and zhoug

title: Authentic Lamb Rogan Josh
description: A deeply aromatic Kashmiri lamb curry with bold whole spices, velvety braised meat, and a rich, ruby-red sauce that begs to be scooped up with warm naan.

ingredients.name: bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks
ingredients.raw: 800g bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks

ingredients.name: fresh coriander, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh coriander, roughly chopped, to garnish

steps: Pat the lamb chunks dry with kitchen paper. In a bowl, combine the yoghurt with ½ tsp salt and massage it into the lamb. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight for best results.

Heat the ghee in a large, heavy-based casserole or Dutch oven over a medium-high heat. Add the black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick and bay leaves. Fry for 60 seconds, stirring, until the spices begin to crackle and smell fragrant.

Add the sliced onions and cook over a medium heat for 18–20 minutes, stirring regularly, until they turn a deep golden-brown. Do not rush this step — properly caramelised onions are the foundation of the sauce.
Stir in the ginger paste and garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Add the Kashmiri chilli powder, ground coriander, ground cumin, ground fennel, ground ginger and turmeric. Stir vigorously for 1 minute, adding a splash of water if the spices begin to stick.

Increase the heat to high. Add the marinated lamb (along with any yoghurt clinging to it) and the tomato purée. Sear the lamb for 6–8 minutes, turning the pieces, until the marinade has dried out and the meat is lightly browned and coated in the spice masala.
Pour in the lamb stock or water and stir to deglaze any caramelised bits from the bottom of the pan. Season with the remaining salt.

Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover with a tight-fitting lid and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes, until the lamb is completely tender and falls easily from the bone.
Remove the lid, increase the heat to medium and cook for a further 10 minutes to reduce the sauce to a thick, glossy consistency that coats the back of a spoon.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Discard the whole spices if preferred. Scatter over the fresh coriander and serve hot with steamed basmati rice or warm naan bread.
_brief: Lamb rogan josh

title: Authentic Butter Chicken with Basmati Rice
description: Succulent tandoor-spiced chicken thighs simmered in a velvety, aromatic tomato-cream sauce, served alongside fragrant basmati rice — a true classic of the Indian table.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.raw: 600g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi)
ingredients.raw: 1 tsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed

ingredients.name: fresh coriander leaves
ingredients.raw: Small handful of fresh coriander leaves, to garnish

steps: Marinate the chicken: In a large bowl, combine the yoghurt, lemon juice, cumin, ground coriander, Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, turmeric, and salt. Add the chicken pieces, mix thoroughly to coat, cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour (or overnight for best results).

Cook the rice: Rinse the basmati rice in cold water until the water runs clear, then drain well. Place in a saucepan with 480ml cold water and ½ tsp salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, stir once, then reduce to the lowest heat setting, cover tightly, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for a further 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork before serving.

Char the chicken: Heat a large cast-iron or heavy-bottomed frying pan over very high heat. Add 1 tbsp oil, then cook the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer (in batches if needed) for 3–4 minutes per side until nicely charred in spots and just cooked through. Set aside on a plate.
Build the sauce base: In the same pan, reduce the heat to medium. Add the butter and let it melt. Add the diced onion and cook, stirring frequently, for 8–10 minutes until deep golden and soft.

Add aromatics and spices: Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Add the cumin, ground coriander, Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, and cardamom. Stir constantly for 1 minute to toast the spices.

Add tomatoes: Add the tomato purée and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the canned tomatoes and chicken stock. Use a wooden spoon to break up the tomatoes. Simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and the oil begins to separate.

Blend the sauce: Carefully transfer the sauce to a blender (or use a stick blender) and blitz until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an ultra-silky restaurant-style finish.
Finish the sauce: Return the pan to low heat. Stir in the double cream, honey, and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
