Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and cook for a further 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the drained potatoes to the pan and press down lightly with a spatula. Cook undisturbed for 2 minutes to begin building a crust.
Add the corned beef chunks, breaking them up slightly with the spatula so they mingle with the potato. Drizzle over the Worcestershire sauce and season generously with salt and black pepper.

Press the mixture firmly into an even layer. Cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes until a deep golden crust forms on the bottom, then fold sections over and press down again. Repeat once more to develop a crust throughout.
Add the butter, allow it to melt, and toss everything briefly to coat. Scatter over the parsley, then reduce the heat to low to keep the hash warm.
In a separate small frying pan, heat the remaining 1 tbsp of vegetable oil over a medium heat. Crack in the eggs and fry for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Divide the corned beef hash between two warm plates, top each portion with a fried egg, and serve immediately.
_brief: Corned beef hash with a fried egg, ready in about 25 minutes

title: Classic Rosemary Shepherd's Pie
description: A hearty, soul-warming British classic of slow-cooked minced lamb and vegetables in a rich gravy, fragrant with fresh rosemary, crowned with a golden, buttery mashed potato crust.

ingredients.name: fresh rosemary sprigs
ingredients.raw: 2 fresh rosemary sprigs, leaves finely chopped

ingredients.name: Maris Piper potatoes
ingredients.raw: 800g Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Preheat your oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan / gas mark 5).

Heat the olive oil in a large, deep ovenproof frying pan or casserole over a medium-high heat. Add the lamb mince and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until well browned. Drain off any excess fat and set the mince aside.
In the same pan over a medium heat, fry the onion, carrots, and celery for 8–10 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, chopped rosemary, and thyme, and cook for a further 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes, then sprinkle over the plain flour and stir well to coat the vegetables.

Return the browned lamb to the pan. Pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce, stirring continuously. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the gravy is thick and glossy.
Stir in the frozen peas and season generously with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, cook the potatoes in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for 15–18 minutes until completely tender. Drain thoroughly and leave to steam-dry for 2 minutes.
Mash the potatoes until smooth, then beat in the butter and warmed milk until light and creamy. Season to taste, then stir in the egg yolk (this helps the topping achieve a golden finish).

Spoon the lamb mixture into a large baking dish (approx. 28 × 20 cm) if not already in one. Top evenly with the mashed potato, spreading it to the edges. Use a fork to create ridges across the surface — these will crisp up beautifully in the oven.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25–30 minutes until the potato crust is deep golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
Remove from the oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh rosemary if desired.
_brief: Shepherd's pie with rosemary

title: British Beef Stew with Herb Dumplings
description: A deeply comforting British classic — slow-cooked tender beef in a rich, glossy gravy crowned with fluffy, herb-flecked suet dumplings.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.raw: 3 medium carrots, cut into chunky rounds

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.raw: 300g Maris Piper potatoes, cut into 3cm chunks

ingredients.name: fresh parsley
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped (for dumplings)

steps: Pat the beef chunks dry with kitchen paper. Season the plain flour generously with salt and black pepper, then toss the beef in the seasoned flour until evenly coated, shaking off any excess.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-based casserole or Dutch oven over a high heat. Brown the beef in two batches for 3–4 minutes per batch, turning to colour all sides. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrots and celery to the same pot and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6–7 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add the Worcestershire sauce, beef stock, bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Stir well, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the browned beef to the pot, along with any resting juices. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potato chunks to the stew, stir gently, replace the lid and continue to simmer for a further 30 minutes until the beef is very tender and the potatoes are cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the herb dumplings: combine the self-raising flour, suet, parsley and thyme leaves in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Gradually add the cold water, mixing with a fork until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Divide into 8 equal balls with lightly floured hands.
Remove the lid from the stew and discard the bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning. Gently nestle the dumpling balls on top of the stew, spacing them evenly.
Replace the lid and cook for 20 minutes — do not lift the lid during this time — until the dumplings have puffed up and are cooked through. For a golden top, remove the lid for the final 5 minutes.
Ladle the stew into deep bowls, ensuring each serving gets two dumplings, and garnish with a little extra fresh parsley.
_brief: Beef stew with herb dumplings

title: Gambas al Ajillo with Crusty Bread
description: Plump prawns sizzled in a fragrant bath of golden garlic, smoky paprika, and extra-virgin olive oil, served straight from the pan with crusty bread to mop up every last drop.

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 400 g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: crusty baguette or sourdough loaf, sliced
ingredients.raw: 1 crusty baguette or sourdough loaf, sliced

steps: Pat the king prawns thoroughly dry with kitchen paper and season evenly with the fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Pour the extra-virgin olive oil into a large, heavy-based frying pan or traditional cazuela (earthenware dish) and place over a medium-low heat.
Add the sliced garlic and chilli flakes to the cold oil, then gently heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently, until the garlic turns pale golden and fragrant — do not let it brown.
Increase the heat to high. Add the seasoned prawns to the pan in a single layer and cook for 1 minute without moving them, until they begin to turn pink on the underside.
Sprinkle over the smoked paprika, then pour in the dry sherry. The pan will sizzle dramatically — this is perfect.
Toss and cook the prawns for a further 1–2 minutes, turning once, until they are just cooked through, pink all over, and curled. Do not overcook.
Remove the pan from the heat immediately. Scatter over the chopped flat-leaf parsley and taste for seasoning, adjusting if needed.
Serve the gambas directly in the pan — or transfer to a warm cazuela — with lemon wedges on the side and plenty of crusty bread to soak up the garlicky oil.
_brief: Gambas al ajillo with crusty bread, ready in about 20 minutes

title: One-Pan Spanish Chicken with Chorizo and Potatoes
description: A rustic, smoky Spanish traybake of golden chicken thighs, sizzling chorizo, and tender paprika-roasted potatoes all cooked together in one gloriously flavourful pan.

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes
ingredients.raw: 600g waxy potatoes (e.g. Charlotte), cut into 2cm chunks

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.raw: 1 large red onion, cut into wedges

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, deseeded and sliced

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: small handful of fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to season

steps: Preheat your oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan / Gas 6).

In a large bowl, combine the potato chunks and red onion wedges with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, the sweet and hot smoked paprika, dried oregano, a generous pinch of flaky sea salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat evenly.
Tip the seasoned potatoes and onions into a large, deep roasting tray and spread into a single layer. Roast for 20 minutes until the potatoes are beginning to soften and colour at the edges.

Meanwhile, pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper and season all over with salt and black pepper. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil in a frying pan over a high heat and sear the chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 4–5 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp. Set aside.
In the same frying pan, fry the chorizo slices over a medium-high heat for 2 minutes until they release their oils and start to crisp. Remove from the heat.
Remove the roasting tray from the oven. Nestle the seared chicken thighs (skin-side up), chorizo, sliced red pepper, and unpeeled garlic cloves among the potatoes.
Pour the dry sherry over everything in the tray, letting it sizzle as it hits the hot pan.
Return the tray to the oven and roast for a further 30 minutes.

Scatter the cherry tomatoes over the tray, pressing them gently among the other ingredients. Return to the oven for a final 10 minutes, until the tomatoes are bursting, the chicken is cooked through (juices run clear), and the skin is beautifully caramelised.
Remove from the oven and allow to rest for 5 minutes. Scatter generously with fresh flat-leaf parsley and serve straight from the pan.
_brief: One-pan Spanish chicken with chorizo and potatoes

title: Fabada Asturiana
description: A soul-warming Asturian stew of butter-soft white beans slow-cooked with smoky chorizo, morcilla, and saffron-kissed broth — rustic Spanish comfort in a bowl.

ingredients.name: dried large white fabes beans (or large butter beans)
ingredients.raw: 500g dried large white fabes beans (or large butter beans), soaked overnight

ingredients.name: panceta or smoked streaky bacon lardons
ingredients.raw: 150g panceta or smoked streaky bacon lardons

ingredients.name: bone-in pork shoulder or smoked pork rib
ingredients.raw: 250g bone-in pork shoulder or smoked pork rib

ingredients.name: white onion
ingredients.raw: 1 large white onion, peeled and halved

ingredients.name: garlic cloves
ingredients.raw: 4 cloves garlic, peeled and left whole

ingredients.name: flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 1 handful flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped, to serve

steps: The night before, place the dried fabes beans in a large bowl and cover generously with cold water. Leave to soak overnight (at least 12 hours), then drain and rinse well.

Place the drained beans in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. Add the chorizo, morcilla, panceta, and pork shoulder as whole pieces — cutting them will cause them to break apart during the long cook.
Add the halved onion, whole garlic cloves, and bay leaves to the pot, then pour in enough cold water to cover everything by about 5cm (roughly 2 litres).
Bring the pot slowly to a simmer over medium heat. As it comes to temperature, skim off any white foam or impurities that rise to the surface with a ladle.
Once simmering, add the olive oil and saffron threads. Stir in the smoked paprika. Reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting so the stew barely bubbles.

Cook uncovered (or with the lid very slightly ajar) for 2 to 2½ hours, gently stirring occasionally. Do not stir vigorously — beans must stay whole. If the liquid reduces too much, add a small splash of cold water (this 'scaring' the beans helps keep their skins intact).
After 2 hours, check the beans: they should be completely tender and creamy inside. Remove the chorizo, morcilla, and pork pieces and slice them into generous rounds or chunks.
Discard the onion halves and bay leaves. Taste the broth and season well with fine sea salt.
Return the sliced meats to the pot and warm through together for 5 more minutes over low heat.
Ladle into deep warmed bowls, making sure each serving gets a good share of beans, broth, and all three meats. Scatter over fresh parsley and serve with crusty bread.
_brief: Fabada — Asturian bean and chorizo stew

title: Classic British Roast Chicken with All the Trimmings
description: A golden, herb-butter roasted chicken served with crispy roast potatoes, honey-glazed carrots and parsnips, buttered greens, stuffing balls, pigs in blankets, and a rich homemade pan gravy — the ultimate British Sunday roast.

ingredients.name: Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and quartered
ingredients.raw: 800g Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and quartered

ingredients.name: goose fat or vegetable oil
ingredients.raw: 4 tbsp goose fat or vegetable oil

ingredients.name: carrots, peeled and halved lengthways
ingredients.raw: 3 large carrots, peeled and halved lengthways

ingredients.name: Savoy cabbage or Brussels sprouts, trimmed
ingredients.raw: 300g Savoy cabbage or Brussels sprouts, trimmed

steps: Remove the chicken from the fridge 30 minutes before cooking to bring it to room temperature. Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan / Gas 6).

Mix the softened butter with the minced garlic, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Gently loosen the skin over the chicken breast with your fingers and push half the herb butter underneath. Rub the remaining butter all over the outside of the bird.

Stuff the cavity of the chicken with the two lemon halves. Place the chicken breast-side up in a large roasting tin and roast for 20 minutes per 500g plus an extra 20 minutes (approximately 1 hour 35 minutes for a 1.8kg bird). Baste with pan juices halfway through.

Meanwhile, parboil the quartered potatoes in salted boiling water for 8 minutes until the edges are just starting to soften. Drain well and shake vigorously in the colander to rough up the edges. Heat the goose fat or oil in a separate roasting tray in the oven for 5 minutes until smoking hot, then carefully add the potatoes, turning to coat. Roast alongside the chicken for 45–50 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden and crispy.

Wrap each chipolata in a bacon rasher to make pigs in blankets and place on a small baking tray. Mix the sausage meat with the breadcrumbs, diced onion, and dried sage, then roll into 6 golf ball-sized stuffing balls and place alongside the pigs in blankets. Add to the oven for the final 30 minutes of the chicken's cooking time.

Toss the carrots and parsnips in a drizzle of oil and season with salt and pepper. Place on a roasting tray and roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once, then drizzle with honey and return to the oven for a final 5 minutes.
Check the chicken is cooked by piercing the thickest part of the thigh — the juices must run completely clear. Rest the chicken, loosely tented with foil, on a board for at least 15 minutes.

While the chicken rests, make the gravy. Spoon off excess fat from the roasting tin, leaving about 2 tbsp of the pan juices. Place the tin over a medium hob heat, add the flour and stir vigorously for 1 minute. Pour in the white wine, scraping up all the sticky bits, then gradually whisk in the chicken stock. Simmer for 5–8 minutes, stirring, until thickened to your liking. Season and strain into a warm jug.
Boil or steam the Savoy cabbage or Brussels sprouts for 4–5 minutes until just tender. Drain and toss with the butter and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Carve the chicken and serve on a large warm platter alongside the crispy roast potatoes, glazed carrots and parsnips, buttered greens, stuffing balls, pigs in blankets, and a generous pour of gravy.
_brief: Roast chicken with all the trimmings

title: Harira — Moroccan Spiced Lentil, Chickpea & Tomato Soup
description: A soul-warming, deeply aromatic Moroccan harira brimming with tender lentils, hearty chickpeas, and ripe tomatoes, perfumed with ras el hanout, cinnamon and a bright squeeze of lemon.

ingredients.name: canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
ingredients.raw: 400 g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: fine vermicelli noodles, broken
ingredients.raw: 50 g fine vermicelli noodles, broken into short pieces

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: fresh coriander (cilantro), roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch fresh coriander (cilantro), roughly chopped

ingredients.name: salt and black pepper
ingredients.raw: salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: crusty bread or khobz, to serve
ingredients.raw: crusty bread or Moroccan khobz, to serve

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and celery and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for a further 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the ras el hanout, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, smoked paprika and cayenne pepper. Stir continuously for 1–2 minutes to bloom the spices in the oil.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, allowing it to caramelise slightly against the base of the pot.
Pour in the canned chopped tomatoes and stir to combine with the spice base. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking down the tomatoes with the back of a spoon.
Add the rinsed red lentils, drained chickpeas and vegetable stock. Stir well, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have completely broken down and the soup has thickened.
Stir in the broken vermicelli noodles and cook for a further 5–7 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Squeeze in the lemon juice and stir through most of the chopped parsley and coriander. Taste and season generously with salt and black pepper.
Ladle the harira into deep bowls, scatter over the remaining fresh herbs, and serve hot with lemon wedges and plenty of crusty bread or khobz alongside.
_brief: Harira — spiced lentil, chickpea and tomato soup

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Apricots and Toasted Almonds
description: A warmly spiced, slow-braised chicken tagine layered with sweet dried apricots, fragrant ras el hanout, and finished with a shower of golden toasted almonds — a true taste of Marrakech.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.raw: 2 cm piece of fresh ginger, peeled and grated

ingredients.name: saffron threads
ingredients.raw: 1/4 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 3 tbsp warm water

ingredients.name: preserved lemon
ingredients.raw: 1 preserved lemon, pith removed, rind finely sliced

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh coriander
ingredients.raw: handful of fresh coriander leaves, to garnish

ingredients.name: couscous or flatbreads
ingredients.raw: couscous or warm flatbreads, to serve

steps: Steep the saffron threads in 3 tbsp of warm water and set aside for at least 10 minutes to bloom.

In a large bowl, combine the ras el hanout, cinnamon, cumin, turmeric, smoked paprika, 1 tsp salt, and a generous grind of black pepper. Add the chicken thighs and toss to coat thoroughly. Leave to marinate for at least 20 minutes (or overnight in the fridge for deeper flavour).

Heat the olive oil in a tagine or large, heavy-based casserole dish over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken thighs skin-side down for 4–5 minutes until deeply golden, then flip and sear for a further 2 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the sliced onions to the same pot and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and lightly caramelised.
Add the garlic and grated ginger, and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the canned tomatoes, chicken stock, saffron water (including the threads), and honey. Stir well to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs back into the sauce, skin-side up. Scatter the halved dried apricots and the preserved lemon rind around the chicken.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover with the tagine lid (or a tight-fitting lid) and cook over low heat for 45 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
While the tagine simmers, toast the blanched almonds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant. Tip onto a plate and set aside.
Remove the lid for the final 10 minutes of cooking to allow the sauce to reduce slightly and concentrate in flavour.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Scatter the toasted almonds and fresh coriander leaves generously over the top and serve directly from the tagine alongside fluffy couscous or warm flatbreads.
_brief: Chicken tagine with apricots and toasted almonds

title: Moroccan Lamb & Chickpea Tagine with Preserved Lemon
description: Tender slow-braised lamb shoulder and golden chickpeas simmered in a fragrant Moroccan spice broth, brightened with silky preserved lemon and scattered with fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks
ingredients.raw: 800 g bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks

ingredients.name: cooked chickpeas (or 1 × 400 g tin, drained and rinsed)
ingredients.raw: 400 g cooked chickpeas (or 1 × 400 g tin, drained and rinsed)

ingredients.name: saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
ingredients.raw: 1/4 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water

ingredients.name: black pepper, freshly ground
ingredients.raw: black pepper, freshly ground, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
ingredients.raw: 1/2 bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

steps: Combine the ground cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, paprika, ground ginger, and cayenne in a small bowl to make the spice mix. Toss the lamb pieces with half the spice mix, a generous pinch of salt, and a grind of black pepper. Leave to marinate at room temperature for at least 20 minutes.
Scrape the flesh from the preserved lemon quarters and discard it. Rinse the rind under cold water, then slice it into thin strips. Set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large tagine or heavy-based casserole dish over medium-high heat. Working in batches, sear the lamb pieces on all sides until deep golden brown, about 3–4 minutes per batch. Transfer the browned lamb to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the pan. Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring frequently, for 10–12 minutes until soft and lightly caramelised.
Stir in the minced garlic and fresh ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the remaining spice mix and stir for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and stock, then stir in the saffron with its soaking water and the honey. Return the browned lamb and any resting juices to the pot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook over low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Stir in the chickpeas and preserved lemon rind strips. Cook uncovered for a further 20–25 minutes, until the lamb is very tender and the sauce has thickened to a rich, coating consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Remove from the heat, rest for 5 minutes, then scatter generously with fresh parsley and coriander.
Serve straight from the tagine with fluffy couscous or warm flatbreads to mop up the sauce.
_brief: Lamb and chickpea tagine with preserved lemon

title: Crispy Falafel Wraps with Tahini Sauce
description: Golden, herb-packed falafel nestled in warm flatbreads with crunchy fresh vegetables and a rich, creamy tahini sauce — a vibrant Middle Eastern classic ready in under 30 minutes.
steps: Drain and thoroughly pat dry the chickpeas with kitchen paper — removing as much moisture as possible ensures crispy falafel.

Add the chickpeas, garlic, onion, parsley, fresh coriander, cumin, ground coriander, smoked paprika, baking powder, flour, salt, and pepper to a food processor. Pulse until the mixture is coarse and holds together when pressed — do not over-blend into a paste.
Scoop the mixture and shape into 12 small, slightly flattened patties using your hands.
Make the tahini sauce: whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, minced garlic, and water in a bowl until smooth and pourable. Season with salt to taste and set aside.

Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, fry the falafel patties in batches for 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden brown and crispy. Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side, or wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave for 20 seconds.
To assemble, lay each flatbread flat and spread a generous drizzle of tahini sauce down the centre. Top with shredded lettuce, tomato slices, cucumber, and red onion.
Place 3 falafel patties on each wrap, add pickled chillies if using, and drizzle over more tahini sauce. Fold or roll the wraps tightly and serve immediately.
_brief: Falafel wraps with tahini sauce, ready in about 25 minutes

title: Fattoush Salad with Grilled Halloumi
description: A vibrant, authentic Lebanese fattoush loaded with crisp vegetables, sumac-dusted toasted pitta, and golden slabs of grilled halloumi drizzled with pomegranate molasses.

ingredients.name: pitta breads
ingredients.raw: 2 pitta breads, torn into rough pieces

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 20 g fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: fresh mint leaves
ingredients.raw: 15 g fresh mint leaves, roughly torn

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Preheat a grill pan or non-stick frying pan over high heat until very hot.
Toss the torn pitta pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt, then toast them in the hot pan for 2–3 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Remove and set aside.
Whisk together the lemon juice, remaining 3 tbsp olive oil, pomegranate molasses, minced garlic, dried mint, 1 tsp sumac, salt, and black pepper in a small bowl to make the dressing.
Combine the romaine lettuce, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, spring onions, parsley, and mint in a large salad bowl.
Pat the halloumi slices dry with kitchen paper. Place them in the still-hot grill pan and cook for 1–2 minutes per side until deep golden grill marks form. Remove from the heat.
Add the toasted pitta to the salad bowl, pour over the dressing, and toss well to coat everything evenly.
Arrange the grilled halloumi slices over the top of the salad.
Finish with the remaining 1 tsp sumac sprinkled over everything and serve immediately.
_brief: Fattoush salad with grilled halloumi, ready in about 20 minutes

title: Musakhan — Sumac Roast Chicken with Caramelised Onions & Flatbread
description: Tender, sumac-spiced roast chicken piled high on golden flatbread soaked with fragrant onions and olive oil — a showstopping Palestinian classic bursting with tangy, earthy depth.

ingredients.name: large white onions
ingredients.raw: 6 large white onions, halved and thinly sliced

ingredients.name: flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: small handful of flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

steps: In a large bowl, mix 2 tbsp of sumac, the allspice, cinnamon, cumin, black pepper, 1 tsp salt, and 2 tbsp olive oil into a spice paste. Score the chicken pieces two or three times down to the bone, then rub the paste all over and under the skin. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight for best results.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan / Gas 6).

Heat the remaining 80 ml of olive oil in a large, heavy-based pan over medium-low heat. Add the sliced onions and ½ tsp salt. Cook slowly, stirring regularly, for 35–40 minutes until deeply golden and jammy — do not rush this step.
Stir the remaining 2 tbsp of sumac into the caramelised onions and pour in the chicken stock. Simmer for 2 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Spread roughly two-thirds of the sumac onions across a large, lightly oiled baking tray. Lay the marinated chicken pieces on top, skin-side up.
Roast in the preheated oven for 40–45 minutes, until the chicken skin is deep mahogany and the juices run clear when the thickest part is pierced (internal temperature 75 °C / 165 °F).
About 5 minutes before the chicken is ready, warm the flatbreads directly on the oven shelf or in a dry pan until pliable.
To assemble, lay the warm flatbreads on a serving platter or board. Spoon the roasted onions from the tray generously over the bread, letting them absorb all the cooking juices.
Place the roast chicken pieces on top of the dressed flatbreads. Spoon over the reserved warm onions, then scatter with toasted pine nuts and chopped parsley.
Serve immediately with a generous bowl of cold plain yoghurt on the side for drizzling.
_brief: Musakhan — sumac roast chicken with flatbread and onions

title: Menemen with Sucuk
description: A sizzling Turkish classic of silky scrambled eggs with spiced sucuk sausage, ripe tomatoes, and sweet peppers — bold, smoky, and ready in minutes.

ingredients.name: sucuk (Turkish spiced sausage)
ingredients.raw: 150g sucuk (Turkish spiced sausage), sliced into rounds

ingredients.name: green Turkish peppers (sivri biber)
ingredients.raw: 2 green Turkish peppers (sivri biber), thinly sliced

ingredients.name: pul biber (Aleppo pepper / Turkish red pepper flakes)
ingredients.raw: 1/2 tsp pul biber (Aleppo pepper / Turkish red pepper flakes)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped, to serve

ingredients.name: crusty bread or simit
ingredients.raw: Crusty bread or simit, to serve

steps: Slice the sucuk into rounds about 5 mm thick. Finely dice the onion, thinly slice the peppers, mince the garlic, and roughly chop the tomatoes.

Heat the olive oil in a wide, heavy-based skillet or a traditional sahan (copper pan) over medium heat. Add the sucuk slices in a single layer and cook for 2 minutes per side until they release their deep red oil and start to crisp at the edges. Remove the sucuk with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pan.
In the same pan over medium heat, add the onion and peppers and sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute to caramelise slightly. Sprinkle in the sweet paprika and pul biber, stirring to coat everything in the spices.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season with salt and black pepper, and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down into a thick, jammy sauce.
Return the sucuk slices to the pan and nestle them into the sauce. Reduce the heat to medium-low.

Crack the eggs directly over the tomato mixture. Using a wooden spoon or spatula, gently fold and swirl the eggs through the sauce in slow, deliberate strokes — do not over-scramble. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the eggs are just set but still soft and custardy.
Remove from the heat immediately. Scatter over fresh parsley and an extra pinch of pul biber. Serve straight from the pan with crusty bread or simit for dipping.
_brief: Menemen with sucuk, ready in about 20 minutes

title: Turkish Lamb Pide Flatbreads (Etli Pide)
description: Boat-shaped Turkish flatbreads loaded with a richly spiced minced lamb filling, blistered to perfection in a screaming-hot oven and finished with a drizzle of lemon butter.

ingredients.name: strong white bread flour
ingredients.raw: 400g strong white bread flour, plus extra for dusting

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 ripe tomatoes, deseeded and finely chopped

ingredients.name: dried chilli flakes
ingredients.raw: ½ tsp dried chilli flakes (pul biber if available)

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.raw: Salt and black pepper to season

ingredients.name: egg yolk
ingredients.raw: 1 egg yolk, beaten with 1 tbsp water (egg wash)

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.raw: 1 lemon, cut into wedges to serve

steps: Make the dough: combine the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl and mix well. Add the olive oil and warm water, then bring together into a rough dough.

Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth and leave to prove in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.

Meanwhile, make the filling: place the grated onion in a clean tea towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Combine the onion, minced lamb, green pepper, garlic, chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, cumin, allspice, paprika and chilli flakes in a large bowl. Season generously with salt and black pepper, then mix thoroughly with your hands until well combined. Fold in the chopped parsley. Set aside.
Preheat your oven to its highest setting (at least 250°C / 480°F / Gas 9). Place two large baking trays or a pizza stone in the oven to heat up.
Once proved, knock the dough back and divide it into 4 equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each piece into a long oval roughly 30 cm × 12 cm (about 3–4mm thick).

Spread a quarter of the lamb filling evenly over each dough oval, leaving a 2 cm border all around. Fold and pinch the two long edges up and over the filling to form a raised border, then pinch the two pointed ends tightly together to create the classic pide boat shape.
Brush the exposed dough border of each pide generously with egg wash.
Carefully slide 2 pide onto each hot baking tray (or bake in batches). Bake for 12–15 minutes until the crust is deep golden and the lamb filling is cooked through and slightly charred at the edges.
Remove from the oven and immediately brush the crust with melted butter. Rest for 2 minutes.
Slice each pide diagonally into portions and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing and a dollop of plain yoghurt alongside.
_brief: Turkish lamb pide flatbreads

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Tender, smoky marinated chicken bathed in a rich, aromatic tomato-cream masala sauce — a true celebration of authentic Indian spicing.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.raw: 500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 4cm chunks

ingredients.name: fresh coriander leaves
ingredients.raw: handful of fresh coriander leaves, to garnish

steps: In a large bowl, combine the yoghurt, lemon juice, minced garlic, grated ginger, ground cumin, ground coriander, Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, turmeric, and salt. Add the chicken chunks, toss well to coat, cover, and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours (or overnight for best results).

When ready to cook, preheat your grill to its highest setting. Thread the marinated chicken onto metal skewers and grill for 8–10 minutes, turning halfway, until lightly charred at the edges and just cooked through. Set aside.
While the chicken grills, melt the ghee in a large, heavy-based saucepan or kadai over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 12–15 minutes, stirring regularly, until deep golden brown.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the onions and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the ground cumin, ground coriander, Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, and turmeric to the pan. Stir constantly for 1–2 minutes to toast the spices in the ghee.
Pour in the tomato passata and add the sugar. Stir well, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil begins to separate at the edges.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the double cream. Simmer gently for 3 minutes.

Slide the grilled chicken pieces off the skewers and add them to the sauce. Stir to coat, season with salt to taste, and simmer for a further 5 minutes to allow the chicken to absorb the sauce flavours.
Meanwhile, rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear, then cook in a pot of salted boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender. Drain well.
Serve the chicken tikka masala over steamed basmati rice, garnished generously with fresh coriander leaves.
_brief: Chicken tikka masala

title: Authentic Saag Paneer
description: Tender golden paneer nestled in a richly spiced, velvety spinach sauce — a classic North Indian dish bursting with warmth and depth.

ingredients.name: fresh spinach
ingredients.raw: 500g fresh spinach, washed and tough stems removed

ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.raw: 2cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated

ingredients.name: green chilli
ingredients.raw: 1 green chilli, finely chopped (remove seeds for less heat)

ingredients.name: kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves)
ingredients.raw: 1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed between palms

ingredients.name: plain rice or naan
ingredients.raw: Plain basmati rice or warm naan, to serve

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Blanch the spinach for 90 seconds until just wilted, then drain and immediately transfer to a bowl of ice-cold water to preserve its vivid green colour. Squeeze out excess water, then blend the spinach to a coarse purée using a hand or countertop blender. Set aside.

Heat 1 tbsp of ghee in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add the paneer cubes and fry for 2–3 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on most sides. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside on a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp of ghee to the same pan over medium heat. Once shimmering, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the diced onion and cook, stirring frequently, for 10–12 minutes until deep golden brown — don't rush this step; the caramelised onion is the flavour foundation of the dish.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chilli. Cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Add the chopped tomato and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring and pressing it down, until it breaks down and the oil begins to separate from the masala.
Add the ground coriander, ground cumin and turmeric. Stir well and cook for 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Pour in the spinach purée and the 60ml of water. Stir everything together, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 5 minutes so the flavours meld.
Stir in the double cream, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi. Season generously with salt and mix well.
Gently fold in the golden paneer cubes and simmer for a further 3 minutes so they absorb the sauce. Taste and adjust salt if needed.
Serve hot alongside steamed basmati rice or warm naan bread.
_brief: Saag paneer with spinach

title: Keralan Prawn Curry with Coconut & Curry Leaves
description: A fragrant, coastal Kerala-style prawn curry bathed in silky coconut milk, tempered with fresh curry leaves, mustard seeds, and warming spices for an authentically vibrant South Indian dinner.

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 400g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: fresh ginger, finely grated
ingredients.raw: 2 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated

ingredients.name: black pepper, freshly ground
ingredients.raw: ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.name: steamed basmati rice or Kerala parotta, to serve
ingredients.raw: steamed basmati rice or Kerala parotta, to serve

steps: Pat the king prawns dry with kitchen paper, season lightly with a pinch of turmeric and salt, and set aside.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide, heavy-based pan or kadai over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add the mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. As soon as the mustard seeds begin to pop (about 30 seconds), add the dried red chillies and curry leaves — stand back as they will splutter.
Add the sliced onion and cook, stirring frequently, for 10–12 minutes until deeply golden and soft.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the minced garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chillies. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the Kashmiri chilli powder, ground coriander, turmeric, and black pepper. Stir continuously for 1 minute to toast the spices in the oil.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5–6 minutes, mashing them down, until they break down into a thick masala paste and oil begins to separate at the edges.
Stir in the tamarind paste and mix well.
Pour in the coconut milk, stir to combine with the masala, and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to allow the sauce to thicken slightly.
Add the seasoned prawns to the simmering curry. Cook for 3–4 minutes, turning once, until the prawns are just pink and cooked through — do not overcook.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt. If you prefer a sharper edge, add a little more tamarind paste.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve immediately with steamed basmati rice or Kerala parotta.
_brief: Keralan prawn curry with coconut and curry leaves

title: Tarka Dal with Steamed Basmati Rice
description: A soul-warming bowl of golden red lentils simmered with tomatoes and finished with a sizzling tarka of cumin, mustard seeds, garlic and dried chilli — served over fluffy basmati rice.

ingredients.name: fresh coriander leaves
ingredients.raw: 1 handful fresh coriander leaves, to garnish

steps: Rinse the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear, then tip them into a medium saucepan with 800ml of water. Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam, then reduce the heat to a steady simmer.
Stir in the turmeric and cook the lentils, partially covered, for 18–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are completely soft and have broken down into a thick, porridge-like consistency.

Meanwhile, rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear. Place in a saucepan with 360ml of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to its lowest setting, cover tightly and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 5 minutes.
While the lentils and rice cook, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced onion and fry for 6–7 minutes, stirring often, until golden brown.

Add the grated ginger and two-thirds of the sliced garlic (reserving the rest for the tarka). Fry for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chopped tomatoes, ground cumin and ground coriander. Cook for 3–4 minutes, mashing the tomatoes, until the oil separates and the mixture is dark and jammy.
Stir the onion-tomato masala into the cooked lentils. Season with salt, add a squeeze of lemon juice and stir well. Keep warm over a low heat, adding a splash of water if the dal is too thick.

Make the tarka: heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil with the ghee in a small frying pan over high heat. When very hot, add the cumin seeds, mustard seeds and dried red chillies. Let them sizzle and pop for 20–30 seconds, then add the reserved sliced garlic and fry for 30 seconds until golden — watch it carefully so it doesn't burn.
Immediately pour the entire sizzling tarka over the dal. Stir it in gently so you keep some of the aroma at the surface.
Fluff the basmati rice with a fork. Serve the tarka dal over or alongside the rice, garnished with fresh coriander leaves and an extra squeeze of lemon.
_brief: Tarka dal with rice, quick and cheap, ready in about 30 minutes

title: Massaman Beef Curry with Potatoes
description: A rich, slow-cooked Thai Massaman curry with meltingly tender beef, creamy coconut milk, and hearty potatoes infused with warm aromatic spices.

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes
ingredients.raw: 400g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 3cm chunks

ingredients.name: white onion
ingredients.raw: 1 large white onion, cut into wedges

ingredients.name: palm sugar
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp palm sugar (or soft brown sugar)

ingredients.name: fresh coriander
ingredients.raw: 1 handful fresh coriander leaves, to garnish

steps: Scoop the coconut cream into a large heavy-based pot or Dutch oven and cook over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until it splits and the oil separates.
Add the Massaman curry paste to the pot and fry in the coconut cream for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until deeply fragrant.
Add the beef chunks and toss to coat thoroughly in the paste. Sear for 3–4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in the coconut milk and beef stock, then add the cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and bay leaves. Stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Add the onion wedges and potato chunks to the pot. Stir gently, re-cover, and continue to simmer for a further 40 minutes, or until the beef is fall-apart tender and the potatoes are cooked through.
Stir in the fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste. Taste and adjust the balance of salty, sweet, and sour to your liking.
Add the roasted peanuts and stir through. Simmer uncovered for a final 5 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.
Meanwhile, rinse the jasmine rice and cook according to packet instructions.
Serve the curry over jasmine rice, garnished with fresh coriander leaves.
_brief: Massaman beef curry with potatoes

title: Authentic Thai Tom Yum Soup with Prawns
description: A fiery, fragrant Thai broth bursting with lemongrass, galangal, and plump juicy prawns — bold, sour, and deeply satisfying.

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 300g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: lemongrass stalks, bruised and cut into 4cm pieces
ingredients.raw: 2 lemongrass stalks, bruised and cut into 4cm pieces

ingredients.name: Thai roasted chilli paste (nam prik pao)
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp Thai roasted chilli paste (nam prik pao)

ingredients.name: evaporated milk (optional, for a creamy tom yum)
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp evaporated milk (optional, for a creamy tom yum)

ingredients.name: fresh coriander leaves, to garnish
ingredients.raw: 1 handful fresh coriander leaves, to garnish

steps: Pour the stock into a medium saucepan and bring to a vigorous boil over high heat.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and bird's eye chillies. Boil for 5 minutes to infuse the broth with their aromatics.
Stir in the roasted chilli paste (nam prik pao) until fully dissolved.
Add the mushrooms and cherry tomatoes, and cook for 3 minutes until just tender.
Add the prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes until they turn pink and are cooked through. Do not overcook.
Season with fish sauce and fresh lime juice. Taste and adjust — it should be a bold balance of salty, sour, and spicy.
If making a creamy tom yum (tom yum nam khon), stir in the evaporated milk now.
Ladle into bowls, discarding the lemongrass and galangal if preferred. Garnish generously with fresh coriander and sliced spring onions. Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
_brief: Tom yum soup with prawns, ready in about 25 minutes

title: Authentic Vietnamese Beef Pho (Phở Bò)
description: A deeply fragrant, slow-simmered beef broth infused with charred aromatics and warming spices, ladled over silky rice noodles and finished with a vibrant tangle of fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.raw: 1 thumb-sized piece fresh ginger, halved lengthways

ingredients.name: flat rice noodles (bánh phở)
ingredients.raw: 400 g flat dried rice noodles (bánh phở)

ingredients.name: beef sirloin or eye of round
ingredients.raw: 200 g beef sirloin or eye of round, very thinly sliced (partially freeze for easier slicing)

steps: Parboil the bones: Place the beef marrow bones in a large pot, cover with cold water and bring to a vigorous boil for 10 minutes. Drain, then rinse the bones under cold water and scrub the pot clean. This removes impurities for a clear broth.

Char the aromatics: Directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill, char the halved onions and ginger until deeply blackened on the cut sides, about 5 minutes. This adds colour and smokiness to the broth.

Toast the spices: In a dry frying pan over medium heat, toast the cinnamon sticks, star anise, cloves, coriander seeds and cardamom pods for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Tie them in a small piece of muslin cloth or place in a metal tea infuser.

Build the broth: Return the cleaned bones to the pot with the brisket, 3 litres of cold water, charred onions, charred ginger and the spice bundle. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a very gentle simmer.

Slow-simmer: Skim any foam or fat from the surface during the first 20 minutes. Simmer uncovered for 2.5 to 3 hours, until the brisket is completely tender. Top up with boiling water if the level drops.

Season the broth: Remove the brisket and set aside to cool slightly. Discard the bones, onion, ginger and spice bundle. Season the clear broth with fish sauce, rock sugar and salt, adjusting to taste — it should be savoury, lightly sweet and deeply fragrant.
Slice the brisket: Thinly slice the cooked brisket against the grain into bite-sized pieces. Keep warm.
Prepare the noodles: Soak the rice noodles in cold water for 20 minutes, then cook in a pot of boiling water for 1–2 minutes until just tender. Drain and divide between 2 large deep bowls.
Assemble the bowls: Arrange sliced brisket and raw thin-sliced beef sirloin over the noodles, followed by sliced spring onions and raw white onion.
Finish with broth: Bring the broth back to a rolling boil. Ladle it generously and piping hot over each bowl — the boiling broth will cook the raw beef slices instantly.

Serve with garnishes: Bring each bowl to the table alongside a plate of bean sprouts, Thai basil, coriander, mint, sliced chillies and lime wedges. Offer hoisin sauce and sriracha on the side for each diner to customise their bowl.
_brief: Beef pho with rice noodles and herbs

title: Authentic Korean Vegetable Bibimbap with Fried Egg
description: A vibrant Korean rice bowl piled high with seasoned vegetables, a golden sunny-side-up egg, and a fiery-sweet gochujang sauce that ties every colourful bite together.

ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp neutral cooking oil (e.g. vegetable or sunflower)

steps: Rinse the short-grain rice in cold water until the water runs clear. Combine with 360 ml water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from heat and steam, lid on, for a further 10 minutes.
Make the gochujang sauce: whisk together the gochujang, honey, rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, and 1 tbsp water in a small bowl until smooth. Set aside.

Blanch the spinach in a pot of boiling salted water for 30 seconds, then transfer to a bowl of ice water. Drain, squeeze out all excess water, and season with ½ tbsp soy sauce, 1 minced garlic clove, and ½ tsp sesame oil. Set aside.
Blanch the bean sprouts in the same boiling water for 1 minute, drain, and season with ½ tbsp soy sauce, ½ tsp sesame oil, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Heat 1 tsp cooking oil in a frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the julienned carrot for 2 minutes with a pinch of salt, then remove. Add another tsp of oil and stir-fry the zucchini for 2 minutes with a pinch of salt, then remove.
Add another tsp of oil to the pan and sauté the shiitake mushrooms with 1 minced garlic clove and 1 tbsp soy sauce for 3 minutes until softened and lightly caramelised. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining cooking oil over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and fry sunny-side-up until the whites are set but the yolks remain runny, about 2–3 minutes.
Divide the hot steamed rice between two large bowls. Arrange the spinach, bean sprouts, carrot, zucchini, and shiitake mushrooms in separate sections around the bowl.
Place a fried egg on top of each bowl. Drizzle with the remaining sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with the gochujang sauce on the side. To eat authentically, add sauce to taste and mix everything together vigorously before eating.
_brief: Bibimbap with vegetables and a fried egg

title: Korean Fried Chicken with Gochujang Glaze
description: Impossibly crispy double-fried chicken wings and drumettes lacquered in a sticky, fiery-sweet gochujang glaze — a true taste of Korean street food at home.

ingredients.name: neutral oil (sunflower or vegetable)
ingredients.raw: 1 litre neutral oil (sunflower or vegetable), for deep-frying

ingredients.name: toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, to garnish

ingredients.name: spring onions, finely sliced
ingredients.raw: 2 spring onions, finely sliced, to garnish

steps: Pat the chicken pieces thoroughly dry with kitchen paper, then transfer to a large bowl. Season with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder, toss well, and leave to marinate at room temperature for 20 minutes.

Make the gochujang glaze: combine the gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, minced garlic, and grated ginger in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir constantly for 3–4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and becomes glossy. Remove from heat and set aside.
Make the batter: whisk together the potato starch, plain flour, and baking powder in a large bowl. Add the egg and ice-cold water, mixing just until a smooth, thin batter forms — do not overwork it.

Pour the oil into a deep, heavy-based pot or wok and heat to 160 °C (320 °F). Working in batches, dip each chicken piece into the batter, let excess drip off, and gently lower into the oil. Fry for 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until pale golden and just cooked through. Remove with a spider or slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack. Repeat with remaining pieces.

Raise the oil temperature to 190 °C (375 °F). Return all the chicken to the hot oil in batches and fry for a second time for 3–4 minutes until deep golden and audibly crackling. Drain again on the wire rack. This double-fry is the secret to ultra-crispy Korean fried chicken.
While the chicken is still hot, transfer it to a large bowl. Pour the gochujang glaze over the top and toss vigorously until every piece is evenly coated and glistening.
Arrange on a serving platter, scatter with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions, and serve immediately alongside pickled radish (danmuji) and cold beer or barley tea.
_brief: Korean fried chicken with gochujang glaze

title: Bún Chả — Grilled Lemongrass Pork with Rice Noodles & Fresh Herbs
description: Smoky caramelised pork patties and belly slices grilled over high heat, served alongside springy rice vermicelli, a fragrant lemongrass-fish sauce broth, and a riot of fresh Vietnamese herbs — the iconic street-food bowl of Hanoi.

ingredients.name: lemongrass stalks, white part only, finely minced
ingredients.raw: 3 lemongrass stalks, white part only, finely minced

ingredients.name: fresh perilla (shiso) or Vietnamese balm leaves
ingredients.raw: 1 large handful fresh perilla (shiso) or Vietnamese balm leaves

ingredients.name: cucumber, cut into thin matchsticks
ingredients.raw: ½ cucumber, cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Make the marinade: in a large bowl, combine the minced lemongrass, garlic, shallots, fish sauce, caster sugar, honey, black pepper and oil. Stir well until the sugar dissolves.

Divide the marinade evenly between two bowls. Add the thinly sliced pork belly to one bowl and the pork mince to the other. Mix both well, cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours for deeper flavour).
Shape the marinated mince into small, flat patties roughly 4–5 cm across (about 8–10 patties total). Set aside.

Cook the rice vermicelli according to the packet instructions (usually soaking in boiling water for 3–4 minutes), then drain, rinse under cold water to stop cooking, and divide into neat nests on a large serving plate.

Make the dipping broth: combine the warm water, fish sauce, rice vinegar, lime juice and caster sugar in a small saucepan. Stir over low heat just until the sugar dissolves — do not boil. Remove from heat, add the sliced chilli and garlic, taste and adjust to your preference (it should be sweet, sour, salty and a little spicy). Pour into two individual dipping bowls.
Heat a charcoal grill, griddle pan or heavy cast-iron skillet to very high heat. Lightly brush the grate or pan with oil.
Grill the pork belly slices for 2–3 minutes per side until deeply charred at the edges and cooked through. Remove and keep warm.
Grill the pork mince patties for 3–4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until caramelised and cooked through with good char marks. Remove and keep warm.
Arrange all the herbs (mint, perilla), bean sprouts, cucumber matchsticks and spring onions on a large sharing plate alongside the noodle nests.

To serve, place the grilled pork belly and mince patties directly into each bowl of warm dipping broth. Serve with the noodles, fresh herbs and vegetables on the side. To eat, dip bundles of noodles and herbs into the broth, picking up pieces of pork with each mouthful.
_brief: Bun cha — grilled lemongrass pork with noodles and herbs

title: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi & Pork Stew)
description: A deeply satisfying, fiery Korean stew of well-fermented kimchi and tender pork belly simmered in a rich, crimson broth — soul-warming comfort food at its most authentic.

ingredients.name: well-fermented napa cabbage kimchi
ingredients.raw: 400 g well-fermented napa cabbage kimchi, roughly chopped

ingredients.name: pork belly
ingredients.raw: 250 g pork belly, cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: firm tofu
ingredients.raw: 300 g firm tofu, sliced into 1 cm slabs

ingredients.name: kimchi brine
ingredients.raw: 3 tbsp kimchi brine (from the kimchi jar)

ingredients.name: spring onions
ingredients.raw: 3 spring onions — whites sliced for cooking, greens reserved for garnish

steps: Heat the cooking oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Korean earthenware pot (ttukbaegi) over medium-high heat. Add the pork belly pieces and sear for 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly golden on the edges.
Add the minced garlic, sliced white onion, and spring onion whites to the pot. Stir-fry with the pork for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chopped kimchi and kimchi brine. Stir everything together and cook for 3–4 minutes, allowing the kimchi to caramelise slightly and meld with the pork fat.
Add the gochugaru, gochujang, doenjang, soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil. Stir well to coat all the ingredients in the seasoning paste.
Pour in the water or dashima stock. Stir to combine, then bring to a vigorous boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes to allow the flavours to deepen and the pork to become tender.
Gently lay the tofu slices on top of the stew. Replace the lid and simmer for a further 10 minutes. Avoid stirring aggressively so the tofu holds its shape.
Taste and adjust seasoning — add more soy sauce for saltiness, gochugaru for heat, or a pinch of sugar to balance.
Scatter the reserved spring onion greens over the top. Serve immediately, piping hot, directly in the pot alongside steamed short-grain white rice.
_brief: Kimchi jjigae — kimchi and pork stew

title: Beef Chow Mein
description: Silky egg noodles tossed with tender strips of beef, crisp vegetables, and a rich, savoury wok sauce — a classic Chinese takeaway favourite made fast at home.

ingredients.name: beef sirloin or flank steak
ingredients.raw: 300g beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain

ingredients.name: bicarbonate of soda
ingredients.raw: 1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda (for velveting the beef)

steps: Slice the beef thinly against the grain, then toss with the bicarbonate of soda, cornflour, and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Set aside to velvet for 10 minutes — this tenderises the meat quickly.

Cook the egg noodles according to the packet instructions (usually 3–4 minutes in boiling water), then drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Mix the sauce in a small bowl: combine the oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and white pepper. Stir well and set aside.
Heat a wok or large frying pan over the highest heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil, then stir-fry the beef in a single layer for 1–2 minutes until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add another tbsp of oil to the wok. Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 20 seconds until fragrant, then add the onion and carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the shredded cabbage and continue stir-frying for 1 minute until just wilted.
Add the drained noodles to the wok and pour over the sauce. Toss everything together vigorously with tongs for 1–2 minutes until the noodles are evenly coated.
Return the cooked beef to the wok along with the bean sprouts and spring onions. Toss for a final 1 minute over high heat.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed, then serve immediately straight from the wok.
_brief: Beef chow mein, ready in about 25 minutes

title: Authentic Chinese Sweet and Sour Pork with Peppers and Pineapple
description: Crispy golden pork pieces tossed with vibrant peppers and juicy pineapple in a glossy, tangy-sweet Cantonese sauce — a true taste of authentic Chinese home cooking.

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, cut into 3cm chunks

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 green bell pepper, cut into 3cm chunks

ingredients.name: pineapple chunks
ingredients.raw: 200g fresh or tinned pineapple chunks (juice reserved if tinned)

ingredients.name: pineapple juice
ingredients.raw: 3 tbsp pineapple juice (from tin or fresh)

ingredients.name: cornflour
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water (slurry)

steps: Combine the pork cubes with 1 tbsp light soy sauce, Shaoxing rice wine, and white pepper in a bowl. Mix well and marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Mix together the ketchup, rice vinegar, caster sugar, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, and pineapple juice in a small bowl to make the sweet and sour sauce. Set aside.
Add the beaten egg to the marinated pork and stir to coat. Sprinkle over 5 tbsp cornflour and toss until every piece is well coated and no wet spots remain.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or deep saucepan to 175°C (350°F). Working in two batches, carefully lower the pork pieces into the oil and fry for 4–5 minutes until pale golden and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper.
Increase the oil temperature to 190°C (375°F). Return all the pork to the oil and fry for a further 2 minutes until deeply golden and extra crispy. Drain again on kitchen paper.
Carefully pour off all but 2 tbsp of oil from the wok. Reheat over high heat until smoking, then stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the red and green peppers to the wok and stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp.
Pour in the sweet and sour sauce and bring to a rapid bubble, stirring constantly.
Add the pineapple chunks and stir to coat. Give the cornflour slurry a quick stir, then pour it into the wok. Stir continuously for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy.
Remove the wok from heat, add the crispy pork, and toss everything together until fully coated in the sauce.
Drizzle over the sesame oil, garnish with sliced spring onions, and serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
_brief: Sweet and sour pork with peppers and pineapple

title: Chinese Salt and Pepper Squid with Chilli and Spring Onion
description: Crispy, golden squid tossed in a fragrant salt and pepper seasoning with fiery chilli and fresh spring onion — a beloved Chinese restaurant classic made right at home.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
ingredients.raw: 2cm piece fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

steps: Score each squid tube by cutting it open flat, then make shallow diagonal cuts across the inside surface in a crosshatch pattern. Cut tubes into roughly 4cm pieces and leave tentacles whole. Pat everything completely dry with kitchen paper.

Toast the black peppercorns and Sichuan peppercorns in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Tip into a pestle and mortar and grind to a coarse powder. Combine with the sea salt flakes, ground white pepper, and five-spice powder. Set aside.
Whisk the egg whites in a bowl until lightly frothy but not stiff. Add the squid pieces and toss to coat.

Mix the cornflour and plain flour together in a separate bowl along with half the salt-and-pepper seasoning mix. Lift the squid from the egg white, letting the excess drip off, and toss in the flour mixture until evenly coated. Shake off any excess.
Pour the vegetable oil into a deep wok or heavy-based saucepan and heat to 190°C (375°F). Test by dropping in a small piece of squid — it should sizzle and rise immediately.
Working in two batches, deep-fry the squid for 2–3 minutes until golden, crisp and just cooked through. Remove with a spider or slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack lined with kitchen paper.

Carefully pour off most of the frying oil, leaving just 1 tablespoon in the wok. Heat over high heat until smoking, then add the garlic, ginger, and chilli. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until just golden and fragrant.
Add the spring onion batons and toss for a further 30 seconds over high heat.
Return all the fried squid to the wok. Sprinkle over the remaining salt-and-pepper seasoning mix and drizzle with sesame oil. Toss everything together vigorously for 20–30 seconds to coat.
Tip immediately onto a serving plate and serve at once, ideally with steamed jasmine rice and a wedge of lemon on the side.
_brief: Salt and pepper squid with chilli and spring onion

title: Chicken Yakitori Donburi Rice Bowl
description: Tender, caramelised yakitori chicken glazed in a sweet soy tare sauce, served over fluffy steamed rice and finished with spring onions and sesame seeds for an authentic Japanese donburi experience.

ingredients.name: nori sheet
ingredients.raw: 1 nori sheet, cut into thin strips, to serve (optional)

steps: Rinse the sushi rice under cold running water until the water runs clear, then place in a small saucepan with 360ml water. Bring to the boil, then reduce to the lowest heat, cover tightly and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 5 minutes.

While the rice cooks, make the yakitori tare: combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake and caster sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from heat and stir in the sesame oil. Set aside.
Cut the chicken thighs into roughly 3cm chunks. Pat dry with kitchen paper — this helps achieve a good sear.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces skin-side down in a single layer and cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy.

Flip the chicken pieces and cook for a further 2–3 minutes until cooked through. Reduce the heat to medium and pour the tare sauce over the chicken. Toss to coat and cook for 1–2 minutes, turning constantly, until the chicken is glossy and deeply caramelised. Watch carefully to avoid burning.
Fluff the rice with a fork or rice paddle and divide between two deep bowls.
Spoon the glazed yakitori chicken over the rice, pouring any remaining tare sauce from the pan on top.
Garnish with sliced spring onions, toasted sesame seeds, and nori strips. Serve immediately with a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi for heat, if desired.
_brief: Chicken yakitori donburi rice bowl, ready in about 25 minutes

title: Chicken Quesadillas with Fresh Pico de Gallo
description: Crispy golden flour tortillas packed with smoky seasoned chicken and melted cheese, served with a vibrant, freshly made pico de gallo.
steps: Make the pico de gallo: combine the diced tomatoes, white onion, jalapeño, and coriander in a bowl. Squeeze over the lime juice, season with 1/4 tsp salt, stir well, and set aside to let the flavours meld.
Slice the chicken breasts into thin strips. In a bowl, toss the chicken with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.

Heat a large non-stick or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add the seasoned chicken strips and cook for 4–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through with a slight char. Transfer to a plate and roughly shred or slice.

Wipe the skillet clean and return it to medium heat. Lay one flour tortilla flat in the pan. Scatter half the shredded cheese evenly over the entire tortilla, then distribute half the chicken over one half only.
Fold the cheese-only side of the tortilla over the chicken side to form a half-moon. Press down gently with a spatula and cook for 1–2 minutes until the underside is golden and crispy.
Flip carefully and cook for a further 1–2 minutes until the second side is golden and the cheese is fully melted. Slide onto a board and repeat with the remaining tortilla, cheese, and chicken.
Cut each quesadilla into 3 wedges with a sharp knife or pizza cutter. Serve immediately alongside the fresh pico de gallo.
_brief: Chicken quesadillas with pico de gallo, ready in about 25 minutes

title: Rich Tonkotsu Pork Ramen with Soft-Boiled Soy Egg
description: A deeply flavourful, milky tonkotsu broth loaded with tender chashu pork belly, springy ramen noodles, and a silky soy-marinated soft-boiled egg — a soul-warming bowl of authentic Japanese comfort.

ingredients.name: pork trotters (split by butcher)
ingredients.raw: 1 kg pork trotters, split by butcher

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen ramen noodles
ingredients.raw: 2 portions fresh or frozen ramen noodles (approx. 300 g total)

steps: Blanch the pork trotters: place them in a large pot, cover with cold water and bring to a vigorous boil for 10 minutes. Drain, rinse each piece thoroughly under cold running water and scrub away any grey scum or impurities. Clean the pot.

Make the soy-marinated eggs: bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Gently lower in the eggs and cook for exactly 6 minutes and 30 seconds for a jammy, soft yolk. Transfer immediately to an ice-water bath for 5 minutes, then peel. Combine 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin and 50 ml water in a small zip-lock bag or bowl, add the peeled eggs and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours (overnight is ideal).

Prepare the chashu pork belly: roll the pork belly tightly into a log, skin-side out, and tie with kitchen string at 3 cm intervals. Sear all sides in a lightly oiled heavy pan over high heat until golden brown, about 5 minutes total.

Build the broth: place the blanched trotters and seared pork belly roll into the cleaned large pot. Add 3 litres of water, the ginger slices, smashed garlic, and 2 of the spring onions. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, then reduce to a vigorous simmer (not a gentle one — you need the agitation to turn the broth opaque and creamy). Cook uncovered for 3 hours, topping up with boiling water as needed to keep the bones submerged.

After 3 hours, remove the pork belly roll and set aside to cool slightly. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding the solids. You should have roughly 1.2–1.5 litres of rich, milky tonkotsu broth. Season with salt.

Slice the chashu: remove the kitchen string from the pork belly. Slice it into 1 cm rounds. For extra caramelisation, sear the slices briefly in a hot dry pan or glaze with a little soy sauce under a grill for 2 minutes.

Make the tare (seasoning sauce): in a small saucepan, combine 80 ml soy sauce, 60 ml mirin and 60 ml sake. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat for 3 minutes until slightly reduced. Remove from the heat and whisk in the white miso paste until smooth.
Assemble the bowls: bring the strained tonkotsu broth back to a vigorous simmer. Stir the sesame oil into the hot broth. Add 2–3 tbsp of the tare to each bowl and adjust to taste.
Cook the noodles according to packet instructions (usually 1–2 minutes for fresh ramen noodles). Drain well and divide between two large, pre-warmed bowls.

Ladle the hot tonkotsu broth generously over the noodles. Arrange 2–3 slices of chashu pork, bamboo shoots and a halved marinated soft-boiled egg in each bowl. Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions, a sheet of nori and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
_brief: Rich pork ramen with soft-boiled egg

title: Slow-Cooked Pork Carnitas Tacos with Pickled Red Onion
description: Meltingly tender, citrus-braised pork shoulder crisped in its own fat, piled into warm corn tortillas and crowned with tangy pickled red onion for a true taste of Michoacán.

ingredients.name: chipotle chillies in adobo
ingredients.raw: 2 chipotle chillies in adobo, plus 1 tbsp sauce

ingredients.name: fresh cilantro (coriander)
ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch fresh cilantro (coriander), roughly chopped

ingredients.name: lime wedges
ingredients.raw: 2 limes, cut into wedges, to serve

steps: Make the pickled onion first: combine the white wine vinegar, water, sugar and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan and bring to a simmer, stirring until dissolved. Place the thinly sliced red onion in a jar or bowl, pour the hot brine over, and leave to cool. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour (or up to 24 hours for deeper colour and flavour).
Preheat your oven to 160 °C (320 °F / Gas 3). Cut the pork shoulder into 4 large chunks, removing any very thick skin but keeping the fat cap on for flavour.

In a large ovenproof Dutch oven or heavy casserole pot, heat the lard or oil over high heat until shimmering. Season the pork chunks all over with the salt and black pepper, then sear in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden brown. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the quartered white onion and smashed garlic to the pot and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until lightly charred. Add the oregano, cumin, and cinnamon and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Return the seared pork to the pot. Squeeze the orange and lime halves directly over the pork, then drop the spent citrus husks in too. Add the chipotle chillies and their adobo sauce, bay leaves, and enough water to come 1 cm up the sides of the meat (around 150 ml).

Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover tightly with the lid and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 3 to 3.5 hours, turning the pork halfway through, until the meat is completely tender and falling apart.
Remove the pot from the oven. Lift the pork pieces onto a large baking tray, discard the citrus husks and bay leaves. Shred the meat coarsely using two forks, leaving some larger chunks for texture.

Pour the braising juices from the pot over the shredded pork. Place the tray under a hot grill (broiler) at 220 °C (425 °F) for 8–10 minutes, stirring once, until the edges of the pork are crispy and caramelised.
Warm the corn tortillas directly over a gas flame for 20–30 seconds per side, or in a dry hot skillet, until lightly charred and pliable. Wrap in a clean towel to keep warm.

Assemble the tacos: top each tortilla with a generous spoonful of crispy carnitas, a tangle of drained pickled red onion, fresh cilantro, and jalapeño slices. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.
_brief: Slow-cooked pork carnitas tacos with pickled onion

title: Huevos Rancheros with Black Beans
description: Crispy corn tortillas topped with smoky black beans, perfectly fried eggs, and a vibrant homemade ranchero salsa — a boldly flavoured Mexican classic on the table in 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: black beans (canned, drained and rinsed)
ingredients.raw: 400 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: jalapeño, finely chopped (seeds removed for less heat)
ingredients.raw: 1 jalapeño, finely chopped (seeds removed for less heat)

steps: Make the ranchero salsa: heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add half the diced onion and the jalapeño and fry for 2–3 minutes until softened. Add two-thirds of the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add the chopped tomatoes, chipotle in adobo, 1/2 tsp cumin, and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 6–8 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down into a thick, chunky salsa. Keep warm on a low heat.

Cook the black beans: in a small saucepan, heat 1 tbsp oil over medium heat. Fry the remaining onion for 2 minutes, then add the remaining garlic, the rest of the cumin, and the dried oregano. Stir for 30 seconds, then add the drained black beans and 3 tbsp of water. Season with salt and heat through for 3–4 minutes, lightly mashing about a third of the beans with the back of a spoon. Keep warm.

Crisp the tortillas: heat the remaining 1 tbsp of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tortillas one at a time for about 30–40 seconds per side until golden and lightly crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate.
Fry the eggs: in the same pan, reduce heat to medium. Add a little extra oil if needed, then fry the eggs to your liking (sunny-side up is traditional), seasoning lightly with salt.
Assemble: place two tortillas on each plate, spoon a generous layer of black beans over each, then lay a fried egg on top. Spoon the warm ranchero salsa over the eggs.
Garnish with sliced avocado, a dollop of soured cream, a scatter of fresh coriander, and a wedge of lime on the side. Serve immediately.
_brief: Huevos rancheros with black beans, ready in about 25 minutes

title: Classic Philly Cheesesteak with Peppers and Onions
description: Thinly shaved ribeye steak piled high with sweet peppers, caramelised onions, and molten provolone cheese, all stuffed into a toasted hoagie roll for the ultimate American street-food classic.

ingredients.name: ribeye steak
ingredients.raw: 400g ribeye steak, sliced paper-thin (freeze for 20 mins first for easier slicing)

ingredients.name: hoagie rolls
ingredients.raw: 2 hoagie rolls (or submarine rolls), split lengthways

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Place the ribeye steak in the freezer for 15–20 minutes — this firms it up so you can slice it paper-thin against the grain with a sharp knife. Set aside.

Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a large cast-iron skillet or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the sliced onions and peppers with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8–10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelised. Add the minced garlic and cook for a further 1 minute, then push the mixture to one side of the pan.

Add the remaining 1 tbsp of oil and the butter to the empty side of the pan and increase the heat to high. Add the thinly sliced ribeye in a single layer. Season well with salt and black pepper, then leave untouched for 1 minute to sear.

Break up the steak with a spatula and toss it together with the peppers and onions. Drizzle over the Worcestershire sauce and stir everything to combine. Cook for a further 1–2 minutes until the steak is just cooked through with no pink remaining.
