Divide the steak mixture into two portions in the pan and lay 3 slices of provolone over each portion. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan with a lid, and allow the cheese to melt completely, about 1–2 minutes.
Meanwhile, lightly toast the hoagie rolls cut-side down in a dry pan or under the grill for 1–2 minutes until golden.
Using a spatula, scoop each cheesy steak portion directly into a toasted hoagie roll. Serve immediately.
_brief: Philly cheesesteak with peppers and onions, ready in about 30 minutes

title: Baked Mac and Cheese with Bacon Crumb
description: A gloriously indulgent all-American baked mac and cheese smothered in a three-cheese sauce and crowned with a golden, smoky bacon breadcrumb crust.

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped

steps: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F / Gas Mark 5) and lightly butter a large 30cm baking dish.
Cook the elbow macaroni in a large pot of heavily salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions (it will finish cooking in the oven). Drain and set aside.

Lay the bacon rashers in a cold skillet, then place over medium heat. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turning once, until crispy and golden. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain, then finely chop. Reserve the pan drippings.
In a large heavy-bottomed saucepan, melt the 60g butter over medium heat. Add the flour and whisk constantly for 1–2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste and form a pale roux.

Gradually pour in the whole milk and evaporated milk, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Continue to cook over medium heat, whisking frequently, for 6–8 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

Remove the saucepan from the heat. Add the cream cheese first and stir until fully melted, then add the grated cheddar and gruyère in three batches, stirring each batch until completely melted and smooth.
Stir in the Dijon mustard, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and cayenne pepper. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Fold the drained macaroni into the cheese sauce until every piece is fully coated, then pour the mixture evenly into the prepared baking dish.

In a small bowl, combine the panko breadcrumbs, chopped bacon, melted butter, and half the parsley. Stir in 1 teaspoon of the reserved bacon drippings for extra flavour, then scatter the crumb mixture evenly over the top of the mac and cheese.
Bake uncovered on the middle shelf for 25–30 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling around the edges and the bacon crumb topping is deep golden brown.

Remove from the oven and leave to rest for 5 minutes — this helps the sauce set slightly so it's gloriously creamy rather than soupy. Scatter over the remaining fresh parsley and serve straight from the dish.
_brief: Baked mac and cheese with a bacon crumb

title: Louisiana Prawn Po'Boy with Remoulade
description: Crispy Cajun-spiced prawns piled into a crusty hoagie roll and slathered with a zingy, creamy Louisiana remoulade — a true taste of the French Quarter in under 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: large raw prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 300g large raw prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: hot sauce (e.g. Crystal or Tabasco)
ingredients.raw: 1 tsp hot sauce (e.g. Crystal or Tabasco)

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped

steps: Make the remoulade: in a bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, whole-grain mustard, hot sauce, lemon juice, minced garlic, capers, smoked paprika, and parsley until smooth. Season to taste, cover, and refrigerate until needed.

Set up the dredging station: in a shallow bowl, whisk together the buttermilk and 1 tsp hot sauce. In a separate shallow bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, Cajun seasoning, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and salt.

Pat the prawns dry with kitchen paper. Dip each prawn into the buttermilk mixture, letting the excess drip off, then dredge thoroughly in the seasoned flour-cornmeal mixture, pressing to coat. Set aside on a plate.
Pour the vegetable oil into a medium heavy-based saucepan or deep frying pan to a depth of about 4cm. Heat over medium-high heat until a cube of bread sizzles and browns in 30 seconds (about 180°C).

Fry the prawns in two batches for 2–3 minutes per batch, turning once, until golden, crispy, and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack or kitchen paper. Season immediately with a pinch of salt.
While the prawns drain, lightly toast the split hoagie rolls under the grill or in a dry pan, cut-side down, for 1–2 minutes until golden.

Assemble the po'boys: spread a generous layer of remoulade on both cut sides of each roll. Layer the shredded lettuce, tomato slices, and dill pickles on the base. Pile the crispy prawns on top, drizzle with a little extra remoulade, and close the roll.
Serve immediately with extra hot sauce and pickle on the side.
_brief: Louisiana prawn po'boy with remoulade, ready in about 30 minutes
